definition_en: staying at the same level or value while conditions change; a quantity whose value does not change

scene: 实验室里，线圈旁的读数在窗外的冷暖变化中始终停在同一格。The reading on the coil stays constant as the room warms and cools.

常数；常量；始终不变的事物

senses.title: A quantity that never varies
senses.definition: a value or quantity that stays the same through every change around it
senses.definitionCN: 在周围一切变化中始终不变的数值或量
senses.example: In the model, the speed of light is treated as a constant.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个模型里，光速被当作一个常量。
senses.why: constant is the adjective 'standing firm' turned into a noun: whatever stands firm is what does not change.
senses.whyCN: constant 是形容词「站得住」转成的名词：凡是站得住的东西，就是不变的东西。

senses.title: Holding one fixed level
senses.definition: remaining at one fixed level rather than rising or falling
senses.definitionCN: 停留在同一个固定水平上，既不上升也不下降
senses.example: The freezer holds a constant temperature of minus eighteen degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 冷冻柜保持零下十八度的恒定温度。
senses.why: the adjective describes a line that does not move; apply it to temperature, pressure or speed and the same flat line appears.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词描述一条不动的线；用在温度、压力或速度上，画出的都是同一条水平线。

senses.title: Never interrupted
senses.definition: happening all the time without a pause
senses.definitionCN: 一直发生，中间没有停顿
senses.example: Constant noise from the road kept the whole street awake.
senses.exampleCN: 公路上持续不断的噪声让整条街都睡不着。
senses.why: a thing that never stops is, seen from another side, a thing that never changes: the noise simply stays on.
senses.whyCN: 从不停止的东西换个角度看就是从不改变的东西：噪声一直就那么响着。

senses.title: Faithful and dependable
senses.definition: staying loyal to a person or a cause over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 在很长一段时间里对某个人或某项事业保持忠诚
senses.example: He remained a constant friend through two decades of trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 二十年的风风雨雨中，他始终是一位忠实的朋友。
senses.why: the oldest English sense is moral steadiness: a person who stands firm does not walk away.
senses.whyCN: 英语里最早的义项是道德上的稳定：站得住的人不会转身走掉。

senses.title: A fixed number in algebra
senses.definition: a number that appears in an expression but is not attached to any variable
senses.definitionCN: 出现在表达式里却不与任何变量相乘的数
senses.example: Add the constant four to both sides of the equation.
senses.exampleCN: 在等式两边都加上常数四。
senses.why: mathematics took the everyday adjective and made it a noun for the part of an expression that carries no variable.
senses.whyCN: 数学把日常形容词变成名词，用来指表达式中不带变量的那一部分。

senses.title: A physical constant of nature
senses.definition: a measured quantity in nature whose value is believed not to change
senses.definitionCN: 在自然界中测得、其数值被认为不会改变的量
senses.example: Planck's constant sets the scale of quantum effects.
senses.exampleCN: 普朗克常数定下了量子效应的尺度。
senses.why: physics extends the same idea to the universe: a number that the world itself does not alter.
senses.whyCN: 物理把这个想法推到宇宙尺度：一个连世界本身都不去改动的数。

senses.title: The constant term of a polynomial
senses.definition: the term of a polynomial that contains no variable at all
senses.definitionCN: 多项式中完全不含变量的那一项
senses.example: The constant term of the polynomial is minus seven.
senses.exampleCN: 这个多项式的常数项是负七。
senses.why: in a sum of terms, the one with no variable is the only term that stays the same for every input.
senses.whyCN: 在一串相加的项里，唯一不带变量的那一项，对任何输入都保持不变。

senses.title: A logical constant
senses.definition: a symbol such as and, or, not or all whose meaning is fixed in a formal system
senses.definitionCN: 在形式系统中意义固定的符号，如「与」「或」「非」「所有」
senses.example: Every logical constant in the proof has a truth-table rule.
senses.exampleCN: 证明中的每一个逻辑常项都有对应的真值表规则。
senses.why: formal logic borrows the word for pieces of language that keep one fixed meaning however the rest of the sentence changes.
senses.whyCN: 形式逻辑借这个词指语言中意义固定的部分，无论句子其余部分怎么变。

senses.title: The one thing always present
senses.definition: a person or feature that is always there in someone's life or in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 在某人的生活或某种局面中始终在场的人或特征
senses.example: The old clock was the only constant in the shifting room.
senses.exampleCN: 在变动不居的房间里，那口老钟是唯一不变的东西。
senses.why: the noun sense widens from numbers to experience: whatever is always there is felt as the fixed point.
senses.whyCN: 名词义从数字扩展到经验：凡是始终在场之物，都会被感受为那个固定点。

intro.en: Constant comes from Latin constans, the present participle of constare 'to stand firm', built on com- 'together' and stare 'to stand'. The mathematical noun is a much later use of the same word.
intro.cn: constant 来自拉丁 constans，即 constare「站稳」的现在分词，由 com-「共同」与 stare「站立」构成。数学上的名词义是同一个词很晚才有的用法。

items.en: Stare meant 'to stand, to stand still'. The deeper Indo-European source is usually reconstructed as a root meaning 'to stand', but that form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: stare 意为「站、站住不动」。更深层的印欧语来源通常被重构为一个意为「站立」的词根，但那是重构形式，不是有记录的实际词形。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus stare gave constare 'to stand together, to stand firm, to remain consistent'; the same verb also meant 'to cost'.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 stare 构成 constare「站在一起、站稳、保持一致」；这个动词同时也表示「值多少钱」。

items.en: The present participle constans described something standing firm, hence steady, unchanging and faithful.
items.cn: 现在分词 constans 描述站得稳的东西，因此指稳定、不变、忠诚。

items.en: English took the adjective through Old French in the fourteenth century, first in the moral sense of steadfast and faithful.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪经古法语引入这个形容词，最早用的是「坚定、忠实」这一道德义。

items.en: The use of constant as a noun for a fixed quantity belongs to the age of symbolic algebra, from the seventeenth century onward; exact first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 把 constant 用作名词指固定量，属于符号代数兴起之后的用法，约自十七世纪起；确切的最早年代为约数。

items.en: The first citation for the mathematical noun is not precisely settled, and the pre-Latin shape of stare is a reconstruction, so both the earliest date and the deepest origin carry some uncertainty.
items.cn: 数学名词义的最早书证年代没有精确结论，stare 在拉丁语之前的形态又属重构，因此最早年代与最深词源都带有一定的不确定性。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for standing; the second group holds words that also mean 'not changing' but with a different focus.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「站立」的拉丁动词；第二组是同样表示「不变」，但侧重点不同的词。

entries.definition: The noun of the quality: the state of staying the same or staying loyal.
entries.definitionCN: 指性质的名词：保持不变或保持忠诚的状态。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning without a pause rather than without change.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，侧重「没有停顿」，而非「没有变化」。

entries.definition: A way of standing, physical or political; it comes from the same standing verb but names a posture.
entries.definitionCN: 指站立的姿势，或政治上的立场；同出那个「站立」动词，但指的是姿态。

entries.definition: Something made to stand upright; the standing root became a name for a carved figure.
entries.definitionCN: 指立着的东西；「站立」词根变成了雕像的名称。

entries.definition: From Latin comes stabuli 'count of the stable', not from constare; the resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁「马厩总管」，并非出自 constare；形似只是巧合。

entries.definition: Likely to stay in place or keep its level; it stresses resistance to disturbance.
entries.definitionCN: 指不容易移动或不易改变水平，强调抗扰动。

entries.definition: Moving or changing at a regular rate, with no jumps; constant can also mean simply unchanging.
entries.definitionCN: 指以规则速率运动或变化、没有突跳；constant 也可以只表示不变。

entries.definition: Fastened or decided once and for all; it points to the act of fixing rather than to a natural level.
entries.definitionCN: 指被固定或一次定死，着眼于「固定」这个动作，而非天然的水平。

entries.definition: The same in every part or at every moment; it emphasizes sameness across space as much as time.
entries.definitionCN: 指各部分或各时刻都相同，强调跨越空间与时间的一致性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: com- 'together' plus stare 'to stand': something that keeps standing exactly where it was.
normal.cn: com-「共同」加 stare「站立」：一直站在原处不动的东西。

normal.en: The family runs constant, constancy, constantly, inconstant and inconstancy.
normal.cn: 同族词有 constant、constancy、constantly、inconstant 与 inconstancy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scientific sense: constant temperature, constant speed, remain constant.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学义：恒定温度、恒定速度、保持不变。

normal.en: The same standing verb underlies stance, statue and stable, all words about standing up.
normal.cn: 同一个「站立」动词还支撑着 stance、statue 与 stable，都是与「立住」有关的词。

normal.en: In algebra a constant is written as a plain number with no variable attached to it.
normal.cn: 在代数里，常数就是一个不带变量的光秃秃的数。

abstract.en: Picture a nail driven into a wall while the wall itself is slowly moving.
abstract.cn: 想象一根钉子钉进墙里，而墙本身正在缓慢移动。

abstract.en: Picture a lighthouse beam that turns all night but never goes out.
abstract.cn: 想象灯塔的光柱整夜转动，却从不熄灭。

abstract.en: Picture a friend who arrives at the same hour every year, whatever else has changed.
abstract.cn: 想象一位每年都在同一时刻到来的朋友，别的一切都已改变。

examples.en: The pressure inside the tank remained constant during the whole test.
examples.cn: 整个测试过程中，罐内压力保持不变。

examples.en: Her constant attention to detail saved the project twice.
examples.cn: 她对细节始终如一的关注两次挽救了项目。

examples.en: In the formula, the constant stands alone with no variable beside it.
examples.cn: 在公式里，常数独自站着，旁边没有任何变量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康」字打头，像「康健地一直站着」——站住不动 → 恒定的、常数

root: 拉丁 constare「站稳、保持一致」= com-（共同）+ stare（站立）；constans 为现在分词「站得稳的」。英语 constant。stare 更早的印欧形态属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all circle one flat line: a level that does not move, a thing that never stops, a friend who never leaves, a number with no variable, a law of nature, a fixed term, a formal symbol, and finally whatever is always there.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都围绕同一条水平线：不动的水平、不停的事物、不走的朋友、不带变量的数、自然的定律、固定的项、形式系统中的符号，最后是那个始终在场的存在。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one flat line cutting through seasons and nights, always at the same height.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条水平线穿过四季与昼夜，永远停在同一个高度。

branches.en: SAME LEVEL: whether a light beam or a freezer, the reading refuses to move.
branches.cn: 同一水平：无论光束还是冷冻柜，读数都不肯移动。

branches.en: UNBROKEN PRESENCE: a noise that never stops and a clock that is always there feel like the same fixed point.
branches.cn: 不间断的在场：从不停的噪声与一直在场的老钟，感觉是同一个固定点。

branches.en: LOYAL STAND: a person who stands firm does not walk away.
branches.cn: 忠诚的站立：站得住的人不会转身离开。

branches.en: NUMBER THAT HOLDS: algebra, physics and the polynomial term each name a value the surrounding changes cannot touch.
branches.cn: 不动的数：代数、物理与多项式的常数项，都指一个周围变化碰不到的值。

branches.en: FORMAL FIXED SYMBOL: logic keeps one meaning fixed while the rest of the sentence varies.
branches.cn: 形式化的固定符号：逻辑让一个符号的意义固定，而句子其余部分可变。

intro.en: Constant is a Latin participle built from a prefix and a verb, and both pieces also build other English words.
intro.cn: constant 是一个由前缀与动词构成的拉丁分词，这两部分还构成其他英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare gives constant, stance, statue, stable and station; com- adds the sense of standing together or standing firm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stare 衍生 constant、stance、statue、stable 与 station；com- 增添「站在一起、站得稳」的意思。

items.example: The prefix makes the standing hold together as one whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀让「站立」合成一个整体。

items.example: The root carries the picture of feet planted on the ground.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着双脚钉在地上的画面。

items.example: The verb also came to mean 'to cost'.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词后来也指「值多少钱」。

items.example: The participle became the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成了英语形容词。

items.example: The level stayed constant for hours.
items.exampleCN: 这个水平持续数小时不变。

items.meaning: the quality of staying the same
items.example: Her constancy reassured the team.
items.exampleCN: 她的坚贞让团队安心。

items.example: The pump runs constantly.
items.exampleCN: 这台泵一直在运转。

items.meaningCN: 多变的；不忠的（否定前缀）
items.example: An inconstant wind made sailing hard.
items.exampleCN: 风向不定让航行变得困难。

items.meaningCN: 坚定；恒常（拉丁性质名词）
items.example: The Latin noun names the same firm standing.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词指的仍是同一种稳稳的站立。

latinEntries.meaning: to stand firm; to be consistent; to cost

definition_zh: 系数；与变量相乘的数；协同因素
definition_en: a number or factor placed before and multiplied by a variable, or a measure of a named property
core_image: 字母旁边挂着一块小牌子，牌子上写着一个倍数
scene: 黑板上，未知项前的小数字被红笔圈了出来。In the equation, the coefficient of the unknown term is three.
sceneCN: 这里 coefficient 指「乘在变量前面的那个数」（第 1 个义项：代数式中与变量相乘的数）；句意为这个等式里未知项的系数是三。图中可辨识物件：黑板、粉笔、被圈出的数字、写在后面的字母。

pos.zh: 系数；常数因子；协同因素

derivatives.zh: 高效的（同出拉丁 efficere，并非由本词加后缀派生）
结果；效果（同出拉丁 efficere）
有功效的（同出拉丁 efficere）

senses.title: The number multiplying a variable
senses.titleCN: 代数式中乘在变量前的数
senses.definition: a number written before a variable that multiplies it
senses.definitionCN: 写在变量前面、与该变量相乘的数
senses.example: In the expression, the coefficient of the unknown term is three.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个式子里，未知项的系数是三。
senses.why: co- 'together' plus efficiens 'working' names what works together with the variable to produce a term.
senses.whyCN: co-「共同」加 efficiens「起作用」，指与变量共同起作用、生成一项的那个数。

senses.title: The leading coefficient
senses.definition: the coefficient attached to the term of highest degree in a polynomial
senses.definitionCN: 多项式中次数最高的那一项所带的系数
senses.example: The leading coefficient is negative, so both ends of the curve fall.
senses.exampleCN: 首项系数是负的，所以曲线的两端都向下走。
senses.why: the coefficient that works with the highest power decides the shape of the whole curve, so it leads the expression.
senses.whyCN: 与最高次幂共同起作用的系数决定整条曲线的形状，所以它「领头」。

senses.title: A binomial coefficient
senses.definition: the number in front of each term when a binomial is raised to a power
senses.definitionCN: 二项式乘方展开后每个项前面的那个数
senses.example: Each binomial coefficient in the row counts ways to choose a subset.
senses.exampleCN: 这一行里的每个二项式系数都在数选取子集的方法数。
senses.why: the number works together with each power of the two terms, and it turns out also to count combinations.
senses.whyCN: 这个数与两个项的各个幂共同起作用，而它同时也数出组合的数目。

senses.title: A measured physical coefficient
senses.definition: a fixed number that relates two physical quantities, such as friction or expansion
senses.definitionCN: 关联两个物理量的固定数，如摩擦或膨胀中的系数
senses.example: Wet ice lowers the coefficient of friction on the road.
senses.exampleCN: 潮湿的冰会降低路面的摩擦系数。
senses.why: physics uses the word for the number that works together with one quantity to predict another.
senses.whyCN: 物理用这个词指与一个量共同起作用、用来预测另一个量的那个数。

senses.title: A correlation coefficient
senses.definition: a number between minus one and one that measures how closely two variables move together
senses.definitionCN: 介于负一与一之间、衡量两个变量共同变动紧密程度的数
senses.example: The correlation coefficient of height and weight was close to one.
senses.exampleCN: 身高与体重的相关系数接近于正一。
senses.why: statistics keeps the 'working together' idea and compresses it into a single number between two limits.
senses.whyCN: 统计保留「共同起作用」的想法，并把它压缩成夹在两个界限之间的一个数。

senses.title: The coefficient of variation
senses.definition: the standard deviation of a set of data divided by its mean
senses.definitionCN: 一组数据的标准差除以其平均数所得的值
senses.example: The coefficient of variation lets us compare spreads across different units.
senses.exampleCN: 变异系数让我们能比较不同单位下的离散程度。
senses.why: the number works together with the mean to state spread without carrying the unit along.
senses.whyCN: 这个数与平均数共同起作用，在不带单位的情况下说明离散程度。

senses.title: The coefficient of determination
senses.definition: the proportion of variation in one quantity explained by another in a regression
senses.definitionCN: 回归分析中一个量的变异被另一个量解释的比例
senses.example: The coefficient of determination showed that the model explained most of the scatter.
senses.exampleCN: 决定系数显示该模型解释了大部分散布。
senses.why: here the coefficient works together with a model to say how much of the variation the model accounts for.
senses.whyCN: 这里的系数与模型共同起作用，用来说明模型解释了多少变异。

senses.title: A stoichiometric coefficient
senses.definition: the number placed before a chemical formula to balance an equation
senses.definitionCN: 写在化学式前面、用来配平方程式的数
senses.example: Changing the stoichiometric coefficient of oxygen balanced the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 改动氧的化学计量系数后，反应就配平了。
senses.why: chemistry writes the 'working together' number directly in front of a formula, exactly as algebra writes it before a variable.
senses.whyCN: 化学把这个「共同起作用」的数直接写在化学式前面，和代数写在变量前面一模一样。

senses.title: A joint cause or factor
senses.definition: something that works together with another cause to produce a result
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个原因共同起作用、产生某种结果的因素
senses.example: Poor drainage was a coefficient in the collapse of the old wall.
senses.exampleCN: 排水不畅是那段旧墙倒塌的一个协同因素。
senses.why: the oldest English use was a person or thing that works together with another, which is the literal sense of the Latin participle.
senses.whyCN: 英语里最早的用法指与另一者共同起作用的人或物，这正是那个拉丁分词的字面意思。

intro.en: Coefficient joins co-, a combining form of Latin com- 'together', to efficiens, the present participle of efficere 'to work out, accomplish'. The mathematical term was coined in the era of symbolic algebra.
intro.cn: coefficient 把拉丁 com-「共同」的合成形式 co- 接在 efficiens 上，后者是 efficere「做成、完成」的现在分词。这个数学术语是在符号代数时代造出来的。

items.en: Facere meant 'to do, to make'. Its compounds are extremely productive in English through words such as effect, defect and sufficient.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」。它的复合形式在英语里极其能产，如 effect、defect 与 sufficient 都出自这条线。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus facere produced efficere 'to work out, bring about, accomplish'.
items.cn: ex-「出」加 facere 构成 efficere「做出来、促成、完成」。

items.en: Co- plus efficiens 'working' formed coefficiens, a thing working together with another; the word was adopted into the new algebra of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
items.cn: co- 加 efficiens「起作用的」构成 coefficiens，指与另一者共同起作用的东西；这个词在十六、十七世纪的新代数中被采用。

items.en: Coefficient entered English mathematical writing in the seventeenth century, naming the number that works together with a variable.
items.cn: coefficient 在十七世纪进入英语数学文献，用来指与变量共同起作用的那个数。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word spread to physics, chemistry and later statistics, always for a fixed number relating other quantities.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词扩展到物理、化学，后来又进入统计学，始终指一个关联其他量的固定数。

items.en: The exact first citation in English and the precise date of the Latin coinage are both approximate; the pieces of the compound, however, are well attested.
items.cn: 英语中确切的最早书证与拉丁语造词的确切年代都只是约数；但这个复合词的两个构件本身都有充分记录。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for doing or making and is easily confused; the second group names other numbers that multiply or relate quantities.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「做、造」的拉丁动词，容易混淆；第二组是其他表示「相乘」或「关联量」的数。

entries.definition: Achieving a result with little waste; it describes a process, not a number before a variable.
entries.definitionCN: 指用很少耗费取得结果，描述过程，而非变量前的数。

entries.definition: The noun for the ratio of useful output to input; it is a kind of coefficient but not the algebraic term itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指有用输出与输入的比值；它是某种系数，但不是代数里的那个术语。

entries.definition: A result produced; it keeps the 'worked out' sense of efficere without the joint prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生的结果；保留「做出来」的意思，但没有「共同」这个前缀。

entries.definition: Built on sub- 'under' plus facere, meaning enough; the similarity to coefficient is only in the ending.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「在下」的前缀加 facere 构成，意为「足够」；与 coefficient 的相似只在词尾。

entries.definition: De- 'away' plus facere, meaning lacking; it is the opposite pole of sufficient, not a partner of coefficient.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「离开」的前缀加 facere，意为「缺乏」；它是 sufficient 的反面，不是 coefficient 的同伴。

entries.definition: Any number multiplied by another; a factor may be a variable or a constant, while a coefficient is the constant part.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何被相乘的数；因子可以是变量也可以是常数，而系数特指其中的常数部分。

entries.definition: The number that does the multiplying; it emphasizes the action rather than the position before a variable.
entries.definitionCN: 指执行相乘的那个数，强调动作，而非写在变量前的位置。

entries.definition: A quantity fixed for a particular case but able to vary between cases; a coefficient is usually fixed within one expression.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某一情形中固定、但不同情形间可变的量；系数通常在一个表达式内固定。

entries.definition: A number that scales a quantity, used in physics and complex numbers; it is close to a coefficient but tied to magnitude.
entries.definitionCN: 指按比例缩放某个量的数，用于物理与复数；接近系数，但更扣住「大小」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin prefix and root, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的前缀与词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: co- 'together' plus efficiens 'working': the number that works together with the variable.
normal.cn: co-「共同」加 efficiens「起作用」：与变量共同起作用的那个数。

normal.en: The family runs coefficient, efficient, efficiency, effect and effective, all from efficere.
normal.cn: 同族词有 coefficient、efficient、efficiency、effect 与 effective，都出自 efficere。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the applied senses: coefficient of friction, correlation coefficient, leading coefficient.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出应用义：摩擦系数、相关系数、首项系数。

normal.en: In algebra the coefficient is the number in front; the variable stands behind it like a shadow.
normal.cn: 在代数里，系数是前面那个数；变量像影子一样跟在它后面。

normal.en: Chemistry writes a stoichiometric coefficient in exactly the same front position as algebra does.
normal.cn: 化学的计量系数写在完全相同的前面位置，和代数一模一样。

abstract.en: Picture a small tag hanging on a letter, and the tag says how many copies of that letter to take.
abstract.cn: 想象一个字母上挂着张小牌子，牌子上写这个字母要取几份。

abstract.en: Picture a lever with a fixed multiplier painted on it: pull once, and the result is doubled.
abstract.cn: 想象一根杠杆上漆着一个固定倍数：拉一下，结果就翻倍。

abstract.en: Picture two causes walking arm in arm, neither enough alone to bring the wall down.
abstract.cn: 想象两个原因挽着手走路，单靠任何一个都推不倒那堵墙。

examples.en: Doubling every coefficient in the equation changes the scale but not the solutions.
examples.cn: 把等式里每个系数都加倍，只改变尺度，不改变解。

examples.en: The coefficient of friction fell sharply once the road was wet.
examples.cn: 路面一湿，摩擦系数就明显下降。

examples.en: A high correlation coefficient does not by itself prove a cause.
examples.cn: 高相关系数本身并不能证明存在因果关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扣一个数」——把一个数扣在字母前面，一起乘起来 → 系数

root: 拉丁 coefficiens「共同起作用的」= co-（共同）+ efficiens（起作用的），后者出自 efficere「做成」= ex-（出）+ facere（做）。英语 coefficient。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep one gesture: a number stands in front of something else and works together with it, whether the partner is a variable, a power, a physical quantity, a data set or another cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项保持同一个动作：一个数站在另一个东西前面，与它共同起作用；这个搭档可以是变量、幂、物理量、数据集，也可以是另一个原因。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small tag hanging beside a letter, showing how many copies of that letter to take.
core.cn: 核心意象：字母旁边挂着一张小牌子，写着这个字母要取几份。

branches.en: THE TAG IN FRONT: the number that multiplies a variable, and the one that leads the highest power.
branches.cn: 前面的小牌：与变量相乘的数，以及领头最高次幂的那个数。

branches.en: COUNTING PAIRS: the binomial coefficient counts how many ways a subset can be chosen.
branches.cn: 数配对：二项式系数数出选取子集有多少种方式。

branches.en: RATIO BETWEEN QUANTITIES: friction and correlation both compress a relation into one fixed number.
branches.cn: 量之间的比值：摩擦与相关都把一种关系压缩成一个固定数。

branches.en: MEASURING SPREAD: variation and determination use the number to say how much scatter a mean or a model explains.
branches.cn: 衡量离散：变异与决定系数用这个数说明平均数或模型解释了多少散布。

branches.en: SHARED CAUSE: chemistry puts the number before a formula, and ordinary speech puts it beside another cause.
branches.cn: 共同的原因：化学把数写在化学式前，日常说法则把它放在另一个原因旁边。

intro.en: Coefficient is a Latin compound of a prefix and a participle; the root is the everyday Latin verb for doing and making.
intro.cn: coefficient 是前缀与分词构成的拉丁复合词，其词根是拉丁语里最常用的「做、造」动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere gives effect, efficient, sufficient, deficient and manufacture; co- adds the idea of working together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 facere 衍生 effect、efficient、sufficient、deficient 与 manufacture；co- 增添「共同起作用」的意思。

items.example: The prefix says the number does not act alone.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀说明这个数不是单独起作用。

items.example: The root is the plain verb of making.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是最朴素的「做」。

items.example: The compound adds the idea of carrying something through.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词增添了「把事做到底」的意思。

items.example: The participle describes what is at work.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词描述正在起作用的东西。

items.meaning: a number working together with a variable
items.meaningCN: 与变量共同起作用的数
items.example: The coefficient of the term is three.
items.exampleCN: 这一项的系数是三。

items.example: An efficient engine loses less heat.
items.exampleCN: 高效的发动机散失的热更少。

items.meaning: the ratio of useful output to input
items.example: The efficiency of the pump fell with wear.
items.exampleCN: 泵的效率随磨损而下降。

items.example: The effect of the drug was slow.
items.exampleCN: 这种药的效果来得慢。

items.meaning: enough, made up to the needed level
items.meaningCN: 足够的（不同前缀，同一词根）
items.example: Sufficient water kept the plants alive.
items.exampleCN: 足够的水让植物活了下来。

derivatives.zh: 结果；效果（同出拉丁 efficere）
有功效的（同出拉丁 efficere）

definition_zh: 指数；幂；上标数字；阐述者；倡导者；典型代表
definition_en: the power to which a number is raised, or a person who sets out and defends an idea
core_image: 一个数字被抬到另一个数字的右上角，像站在肩膀上
scene: 墙上的公式里，一个数字被抬到字母的右上角，表示连乘的次数。In the formula, the exponent tells how many times the base is used as a factor.
sceneCN: 这里 exponent 指「幂指数，即底数连乘的次数」（第 1 个义项：指数）；句意为公式里的指数说明底数被当作因子用了几次。图中可辨识物件：公式、抬高的数字、粉笔、墙面。

pos.zh: 指数；幂；上标数字；阐述者；倡导者；典型

derivatives.zh: 详述；阐述（同出拉丁 exponere）
使暴露；揭露（同出拉丁 exponere）

senses.title: The power a number is raised to
senses.definition: the number that says how many times a base is multiplied by itself
senses.definitionCN: 说明底数自乘多少次的数
senses.example: In the formula, the exponent tells how many times the base is used as a factor.
senses.exampleCN: 在公式里，指数说明底数被当作因子用了几次。
senses.why: exponere means 'to set out'; the exponent sets out how many repetitions the base undergoes.
senses.whyCN: exponere 意为「摆出来」；指数就是把底数重复多少次「摆出来」。

senses.title: The raised figure in notation
senses.definition: the small figure written above and to the right of a base
senses.definitionCN: 写在底数右上方的小数字
senses.example: A raised exponent beside the letter marks repeated multiplication.
senses.exampleCN: 字母旁边抬高的指数标出重复相乘。
senses.why: the written position is the visual form of the mathematical idea: the number is literally lifted above the base.
senses.whyCN: 书写位置正是数学想法的可视化：这个数确实被抬到底数上方。

senses.title: A person who explains
senses.definition: someone who sets out and explains a subject in detail
senses.definitionCN: 把某个主题详细摆出来并加以解释的人
senses.example: He became the clearest exponent of the new method in his department.
senses.exampleCN: 他成了本部门里把这种新方法讲得最清楚的人。
senses.why: the Latin participle meant 'setting forth', and a person who sets a subject forth is an expounder.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁分词意为「摆出来」，把主题摆出来的人就是阐述者。

senses.title: A spokesman for a cause
senses.definition: a person who speaks publicly in support of an idea or movement
senses.definitionCN: 公开为某种理念或运动说话的人
senses.example: She was the leading exponent of the reform movement.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这场改革运动的主要代表人物。
senses.why: from explaining a subject it is a short step to speaking for it, so exponent took on the role of public advocate.
senses.whyCN: 从解释一个主题到为它说话只差一步，于是 exponent 承担起公开倡导者的角色。

senses.title: A typical example
senses.definition: a person or thing that shows what a class or style is like
senses.definitionCN: 能显示某一类别或风格是什么样的人或物
senses.example: The little chapel is a fine exponent of the local stone style.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小礼拜堂是当地石构风格的一个很好例证。
senses.why: a thing that sets forth a style is itself the showing of that style, hence 'a typical example'.
senses.whyCN: 把一种风格摆出来的东西，本身就是那种风格的展示，因此引申为「典型例证」。

senses.title: The exponent of a group
senses.definition: the smallest positive power that sends every element of a group to the identity
senses.definitionCN: 使群中每个元素都化为单位元的最小正整数次幂
senses.example: The exponent of the group divides the order of the group.
senses.exampleCN: 这个群的指数整除群的阶。
senses.why: group theory reuses the arithmetic word for the power that makes every element collapse to the identity.
senses.whyCN: 群论把这个算术词挪用来指那个让每个元素都塌回单位元的幂。

senses.title: The exponent of a prime in a factorization
senses.definition: the number showing how many times a prime factor occurs in an integer
senses.definitionCN: 表示某个素因子在一个整数里出现几次的数
senses.example: The exponent of two in twelve is two.
senses.exampleCN: 在十二里，因子二的指数是二。
senses.why: factorization counts repetitions, and the exponent is exactly the written count of those repetitions.
senses.whyCN: 分解数的是重复次数，而指数正是这些重复次数被写下来的结果。

senses.title: A unit that realizes a linguistic feature
senses.definition: a sound or form that carries a particular grammatical feature
senses.definitionCN: 承载某一语法特征的具体语音或形式
senses.example: The past-tense ending is the exponent of tense in that verb.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个动词里，过去时词尾是时态的体现形式。
senses.why: linguistics borrows the 'setting forth' idea: a form sets forth an abstract feature in audible shape.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借用了「摆出来」的想法：某个形式把抽象特征以可听见的形态摆出来。

senses.title: The exponent in scientific notation
senses.definition: the power of ten that scales a number in scientific notation
senses.definitionCN: 科学记数法中用来缩放数值的十的幂
senses.example: Changing the exponent moved the decimal point six places.
senses.exampleCN: 改变指数把小数点移动了六位。
senses.why: in scientific notation the exponent is the part that records how far the decimal point has been shifted.
senses.whyCN: 在科学记数法里，指数就是记录小数点被移动了多远的那个部分。

intro.en: Exponent comes from Latin exponens, the present participle of exponere 'to put out, set forth, explain', built on ex- 'out' and ponere 'to put, place'. The mathematical sense was added in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: exponent 来自拉丁 exponens，即 exponere「摆出来、陈述、解释」的现在分词，由 ex-「出」与 ponere「放、置」构成。数学义是十七世纪才加上的。

items.en: Ponere meant 'to put, place, set'. It is one of the most productive Latin verbs in English compounds: component, postpone, compose and deposit all descend from it.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放、置、摆」。它是英语复合词中最能产的拉丁动词之一：component、postpone、compose 与 deposit 都出自它。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus ponere gave exponere 'to put out, set forth, expose, explain'. The same verb produced both expose and expound in English.
items.cn: ex-「出」加 ponere 构成 exponere「摆出来、陈述、暴露、解释」。同一个动词在英语里既产生 expose，也产生 expound。

items.en: The present participle exponens named one who sets something forth, hence an expounder or interpreter.
items.cn: 现在分词 exponens 指把某事物摆出来的人，因此是阐述者、解释者。

items.en: English took exponent first as a noun for a person who explains or interprets a text or doctrine.
items.cn: 英语最初把 exponent 用作名词，指解释或诠释文本、教义的人。

items.en: In the seventeenth century the word was applied to the raised number that shows a power, since it 'sets forth' how many times the base is repeated.
items.cn: 十七世纪时，这个词被用来指右上角表示幂的数，因为它把底数重复了多少次「摆出来」。

items.en: The exact first mathematical citation is approximate; the Latin verb itself and its participle are securely attested.
items.cn: 数学义的最早确切书证年代为约数；但这个拉丁动词及其分词本身有可靠记录。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb ponere 'to put' and is a constant source of confusion; the second group names people or numbers with a comparable role.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁动词 ponere「放」，是持续不断的混淆来源；第二组是角色相近的人或数。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus ponere: a part put together with others into a whole; it is not an exponent.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「共同」的前缀加 ponere：与其他部分拼成整体的一个部件；并非指数。

entries.definition: Post- 'after' plus ponere: to put something off to a later time.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「之后」的前缀加 ponere：把事情放到更晚的时间。

entries.definition: Also from exponere, but through French: to put something out where it can be seen, hence to uncover.
entries.definitionCN: 同样出自 exponere，但经法语而来：把东西摆到能被看见的地方，因此指揭露、暴露。

entries.definition: From exponere through Old French: to set out an idea at length; it is the verb behind the 'explainer' sense of exponent.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 exponere，经古法语而来：详细陈述一个想法；它正是 exponent「阐述者」义背后的动词。

entries.definition: Ob- 'against' plus ponere: one who sets himself against another, not one who sets a subject forth.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「对着」的前缀加 ponere：把自己摆到别人对面的人，而非把主题摆出来的人。

entries.definition: In arithmetic, the result of repeated multiplication or the number of repetitions; it overlaps with exponent but can also mean the result.
entries.definitionCN: 在算术里指重复相乘的结果或次数；与指数重叠，但也常指结果本身。

entries.tag: another name for the raised number
entries.definition: A synonym for exponent in older mathematical writing; it also means a pointer or a list.
entries.definitionCN: 较老的数学文献里是 exponent 的同义词；它另指指针或索引。

entries.definition: A person who argues publicly for a cause; it matches the 'spokesman' sense without the explanatory tone.
entries.definitionCN: 公开为某项事业辩护的人；对应「代言人」义，但不带解释的色彩。

entries.definition: One who puts a proposal forward; it is built on the same putting verb, ponere.
entries.definitionCN: 提出并支持某项主张的人；同样由那个表示「放」的动词构成。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: ex- 'out' plus ponere 'put': the exponent is the number put out above the base.
normal.cn: ex-「出」加 ponere「放」：指数就是被放到底数上方的那个数。

normal.en: The family runs exponent, exponential, exponentially, exponentiation and expound.
normal.cn: 同族词有 exponent、exponential、exponentially、exponentiation 与 expound。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the two lives of the word: fractional exponent, and chief exponent of a movement.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出这个词的两条命：分数指数，以及某项运动的主要倡导者。

normal.en: The same ponere builds component, postpone and opponent, all about placing something somewhere.
normal.cn: 同一个 ponere 还构成 component、postpone 与 opponent，都是把某物放到某处。

normal.en: In a power, the base carries the weight and the exponent rides on its shoulder.
normal.cn: 在幂里，底数扛着重量，指数骑在它肩上。

abstract.en: Picture a small figure standing on a tall number's shoulder, counting how many times it is copied.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小人站在一个大数的肩膀上，数它被复制了多少次。

abstract.en: Picture a lecturer lifting a heavy idea above the crowd so everyone can see it.
abstract.cn: 想象一位讲演者把一个沉重的想法举过人群头顶，让所有人都看见。

abstract.en: Picture a label on a bottle that tells you how concentrated the contents are.
abstract.cn: 想象瓶子上贴着标签，告诉你里面的东西浓缩到什么程度。

examples.en: A negative exponent turns the base into a fraction.
examples.cn: 负指数会把底数变成一个分数。

examples.en: She became the public exponent of a quieter style of architecture.
examples.cn: 她成了那种更安静的建筑风格的公开倡导者。

examples.en: The exponent on the ten shows how far the decimal point has moved.
examples.cn: 十上面的指数显示小数点移动了多远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一克斯破能」——把「能」一层层破开叠到右上角 → 指数

root: 拉丁 exponere「摆出来、陈述」= ex-（出）+ ponere（放、置）→ exponens「摆出来的人／摆出来的东西」。英语 exponent，数学义十七世纪起。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses split between two gestures: a number lifted above a base, and a person who lifts an idea into public view. Both come from the same Latin verb for setting something out.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项分成两个动作：一个数被抬到底数上方，一个人把一个想法抬到公众眼前。两者都出自同一个表示「摆出来」的拉丁动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one number standing on the shoulder of another, counting repetitions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个数站在另一个数的肩膀上，数重复的次数。

branches.en: RAISED POWER: the count of repetitions and the small figure written above the base.
branches.cn: 抬高的幂：重复的次数，以及写在底数上方的小数字。

branches.en: PERSON WHO EXPLAINS: one who sets a subject out in detail.
branches.cn: 解释的人：把主题详细摆出来的人。

branches.en: SPEAKING SAMPLE: the advocate speaks for a movement, and the little chapel speaks for a style.
branches.cn: 会说话的样本：倡导者为运动说话，小礼拜堂为一种风格说话。

branches.en: COUNTING POWER: group theory and prime factorization both use the raised number as a tally.
branches.cn: 计数的幂：群论与素因子分解都把那个抬高的数当作计数。

branches.en: REALIZED FORM: a suffix carries an abstract feature, and a power of ten carries a shifted decimal point.
branches.cn: 体现出来的形式：词尾承载抽象特征，十的幂承载被移动的小数点。

intro.en: Exponent is a Latin participle of a verb built from a prefix and the common verb for placing; the same pieces build many English words.
intro.cn: exponent 是一个拉丁分词，其动词由前缀与那个最常用的「放」动词构成；这些构件还构成许多英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere gives component, postpone, compose, deposit and opponent; ex- adds the sense of putting something out into view.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ponere 衍生 component、postpone、compose、deposit 与 opponent；ex- 增添「把东西摆到可见处」的意思。

items.example: The prefix pulls the idea out where it can be seen.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把想法拉到能被看见的地方。

items.example: The root is the plain act of placing something.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是放置东西的朴素动作。

items.meaning: to put out, set forth, explain
items.example: The verb covers both exposing and explaining.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词既包括暴露，也包括解释。

items.meaning: setting forth; one who sets forth
items.example: The participle became both adjective and noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词既作形容词，也作名词。

items.example: The exponent sits above the base.
items.exampleCN: 指数坐在底数上方。

items.example: The curve is exponential in shape.
items.exampleCN: 这条曲线在形状上是指数的。

items.meaning: the operation of raising to a power
items.example: Exponentiation grows faster than multiplication.
items.exampleCN: 求幂比乘法增长得快。

items.meaning: a part placed together with others
items.meaningCN: 与其他部分拼在一起的部件
items.example: Each component was tested alone.
items.exampleCN: 每个部件都单独测试过。

items.example: They postponed the launch by a week.
items.exampleCN: 他们把发射推迟了一周。

core_image: 一条曲线在右端几乎竖直上冲，越走越陡
scene: 一张曲线图上，细线过了某一天后几乎竖直上冲。The curve shows exponential growth after the first week of the outbreak.
sceneCN: 这里 exponential 指「按指数规律增长，即每过一段就乘上同一个倍数」（第 3 个义项：指数式增长）；句意为疫情第一周之后，曲线呈现指数增长。图中可辨识物件：坐标轴、向上弯的曲线、标尺、图钉。

senses.title: Relating to an exponent
senses.definition: connected with an exponent, the raised number that shows a power
senses.definitionCN: 与幂指数那个抬高的数有关的
senses.example: The exponential notation places the power above the base.
senses.exampleCN: 指数记法把幂写底数上方。
senses.why: the adjective simply says 'of an exponent', and the base word is the Latin participle for setting something out.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只说「属于指数的」，而它的基词正是那个表示「摆出来」的拉丁分词。

senses.title: Having a variable in the exponent
senses.definition: describing an expression in which the variable appears in the exponent rather than the base
senses.definitionCN: 描述变量出现在指数位置而不是底数位置的表达式
senses.example: An exponential equation cannot be solved by simple factoring.
senses.exampleCN: 指数方程不能靠简单的因式分解来解。
senses.why: what makes such an equation exponential is precisely that the unknown has climbed into the exponent.
senses.whyCN: 这类方程之所以称为指数的，正因为未知数爬到了指数位置上。

senses.title: The exponential function
senses.definition: a function in which a fixed base is raised to a variable power
senses.definitionCN: 以固定底数取变量次幂的函数
senses.example: The exponential describes growth proportional to the current amount.
senses.exampleCN: 指数函数描述与当前数量成正比的增长。
senses.why: the function is named by the piece that varies, the exponent, rather than by the fixed base.
senses.whyCN: 这个函数以变化的那一部分命名，也就是指数，而不是固定的底数。

senses.title: Exponential growth
senses.definition: growth in which the amount keeps being multiplied by the same factor
senses.definitionCN: 每次都用同一个倍数乘上去的增长
senses.example: Bacteria in a warm dish show exponential growth at first.
senses.exampleCN: 温盘里的细菌起初呈指数增长。
senses.why: when each step multiplies by a constant factor, the exponent rises steadily, so the word for the exponent names the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 当每一步都乘上同一个常数倍数时，指数稳步上升，于是指数的名字成了这种模式的名字。

senses.title: Exponential decay
senses.definition: a fall in which the amount keeps being divided by the same factor
senses.definitionCN: 每次都被同一个倍数除下去、不断减少的过程
senses.example: The radioactivity of the sample follows exponential decay.
senses.exampleCN: 样品的放射性遵循指数衰减。
senses.why: decay mirrors growth: the exponent goes down at a steady rate, so the same adjective covers both directions.
senses.whyCN: 衰减是增长的镜像：指数按稳定速率下降，因此同一个形容词覆盖两个方向。

senses.title: The exponential distribution
senses.definition: a probability distribution that describes the waiting time between events occurring at a constant rate
senses.definitionCN: 描述以恒定速率发生的事件之间等待时间的概率分布
senses.example: The waiting times at the call centre fit an exponential distribution.
senses.exampleCN: 呼叫中心的等待时间符合指数分布。
senses.why: the distribution's curve falls away like an exponential decay, so statistics borrowed the adjective for it.
senses.whyCN: 这条分布的曲线像指数衰减一样往下掉，统计因此借用了这个形容词。

senses.title: Exponential smoothing
senses.definition: a forecasting method that gives recent observations exponentially greater weight
senses.definitionCN: 给近期观测值按指数递减的权重、用来预测的方法
senses.example: Exponential smoothing tracks the sales trend without chasing every spike.
senses.exampleCN: 指数平滑能跟踪销售趋势，又不去追每一个尖峰。
senses.why: the weights fall off in an exponential pattern, so the method is named after the shape of its weighting.
senses.whyCN: 权重按指数形态递减，这个方法便以其权重的形状命名。

senses.title: Exponential running time
senses.definition: describing an algorithm whose running time grows exponentially with the size of its input
senses.definitionCN: 描述运行时间随输入规模按指数增长的算法
senses.example: The brute-force search runs in exponential time on large inputs.
senses.exampleCN: 这种穷举搜索在大输入上以指数时间运行。
senses.why: computer science counts steps; when the count doubles with each added item, the growth is exponential.
senses.whyCN: 计算机科学数的是步数；每多一个数据步数就翻倍，这种增长就是指数的。

senses.title: The exponential as a noun
senses.definition: the exponential function itself, used as a noun in mathematics
senses.definitionCN: 数学中直接作名词用的指数函数
senses.example: The exponential turns addition into multiplication.
senses.exampleCN: 指数函数把加法变成乘法。
senses.why: mathematicians routinely drop the word function and let the adjective stand alone as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 数学家习惯省掉「函数」二字，让这个形容词直接当名词用。

intro.en: Exponential is English exponent plus the adjective suffix -al. The base goes back to Latin exponere 'to set forth', and the mathematical use dates from the age of calculus.
intro.cn: exponential 是英语 exponent 加形容词后缀 -al 构成。其基词上溯到拉丁 exponere「摆出来」，数学用法则始于微积分时代。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus ponere 'to put' gave exponere 'to set out, explain'; the participle exponens became English exponent.
items.cn: ex-「出」加 ponere「放」构成 exponere「摆出来、解释」；分词 exponens 成为英语 exponent。

items.en: Exponent entered English as a noun for an explainer, and only later acquired the mathematical sense of a raised power.
items.cn: exponent 最初以「解释者」的名词身份进入英语，后来才获得「幂指数」的数学义。

items.en: The Latin adjective ending -alis, through French -al, turns a noun into an adjective of relation; exponent plus -al gives exponential.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词词尾 -alis 经法语 -al，把名词变成表示关系的形容词；exponent 加 -al 得 exponential。

items.en: From the late seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the adjective named functions and equations in which the variable sits in the exponent.
items.cn: 从十七世纪末到十八世纪，这个形容词用来指变量位于指数位置的函数与方程。

items.en: During the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word spread to decay, probability distributions, forecasting and computing, always naming growth or fall by a constant factor.
items.cn: 在十九、二十世纪，这个词扩展到衰变、概率分布、预测与计算，始终指按固定倍数增长或下降。

items.en: The exact first date for each applied sense is approximate; the morphological pieces are fully attested.
items.cn: 每个应用义的确切首见年代都是约数；构词的两个部分则有充分记录。

note.en: The first group shares the exponent stem and is easily misread; the second group names other ways of describing rapid or steady change.
note.cn: 第一组共享 exponent 这个词干，容易被误读；第二组是描述快速或稳定变化的其他说法。

entries.definition: The raised number itself or an advocate; the adjective exponential adds the sense of a pattern of change.
entries.definitionCN: 指那个抬高的数，或指倡导者；形容词 exponential 则加上「变化模式」的意思。

entries.definition: The operation of raising to a power, not the shape of a growth curve.
entries.definitionCN: 指求幂这个运算，而非增长曲线的形状。

entries.definition: From expandere 'to spread out', built on pandere, not ponere: it means wide or open, not growing by a factor.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 expandere「铺开」，词根是 pandere 而非 ponere：意为宽广、开阔，不是按倍数增长。

entries.definition: From expendere 'to weigh out, pay', built on pendere: it means costly, not fast-growing.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 expendere「称出、支付」，词根是 pendere：意为昂贵，不是快速增长。

entries.definition: A rare word meaning able to be explained, from the same exponere; it has nothing to do with growth.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见词，意为「可解释的」，同出 exponere；与增长无关。

entries.definition: Simply fast; it says nothing about the rule by which the amount increases.
entries.definitionCN: 只表示快，不说明数量按什么规则增加。

entries.definition: Describes a sudden burst of growth; exponential describes a steady multiplication that eventually looks like a burst.
entries.definitionCN: 描述突然爆发的增长；exponential 描述一种稳定的倍数增长，最终看起来像爆发。

entries.definition: In growth language, geometric increase also multiplies by a fixed factor; the two terms often coincide, though geometric is the older label.
entries.definitionCN: 在增长语境里，几何增长同样按固定倍数相乘；两个说法常常重合，只是几何一词更老。

entries.definition: Speeding up in general; exponential growth is one specific rule that produces acceleration.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指越来越快；指数增长是产生加速度的一种具体规则。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Exponent plus -al: the adjective of the raised number, then the name of the curve it produces.
normal.cn: exponent 加 -al：先是指数这个数的形容词，再成为它所画出的曲线的名字。

normal.en: The family runs exponent, exponential, exponentially, exponentiation and exponentiate.
normal.cn: 同族词有 exponent、exponential、exponentially、exponentiation 与 exponentiate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the applications: exponential growth, exponential decay, exponential distribution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出应用场景：指数增长、指数衰减、指数分布。

normal.en: Exponential growth doubles, then doubles again; each doubling is short Scotch tape on the same stack.
normal.cn: 指数增长翻一倍，再翻一倍；每次翻倍都是往同一摞上再贴一层。

normal.en: Exponential decay is the same tape being peeled off at a steady fraction each step.
normal.cn: 指数衰减则是每一步都按固定比例撕掉一层同样的胶带。

abstract.en: Picture a curve that looks lazy for a long time, then suddenly stands up on its tail.
abstract.cn: 想象一条曲线长期懒洋洋地躺着，然后突然用尾巴立起来。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour that doubles its listeners every hour, until the room cannot hold them.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻每过一小时听众人数就翻倍，直到房间装不下。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of coffee cooling by the same fraction every minute, never quite reaching room temperature.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯咖啡每分钟按同一比例降温，永远差一点才到室温。

examples.en: The number of cases showed exponential growth before the restrictions began.
examples.cn: 限制措施开始前，病例数呈指数增长。

examples.en: The exponential decay of the signal made the far stations inaudible.
examples.cn: 信号的指数衰减让远处的台听不见了。

examples.en: That algorithm is exponential, so it is useless once the list gets long.
examples.cn: 那个算法是指数级的，列表一长就没用了。

root: 英语 exponent（指数，源自拉丁 exponens「摆出来的」）+ 形容词后缀 -al。拉丁词根为 exponere = ex-（出）+ ponere（放）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one shape: a number placed above a base, then the function built from it, then the curve that doubles or halves by a fixed factor, and finally the places where that curve appears in data and machines.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项顺着同一个形状展开：一个数被放到基座上方，然后是由它构成的函数，再是那个按固定倍数翻倍或减半的曲线，最后是这条曲线在数据与机器里出现的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curve that looks almost flat and then stands up on its tail.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条起初几乎是平的，后来用尾巴立起来的曲线。

branches.en: THE RAISED NUMBER: the adjective belongs to the exponent, and to equations where the unknown sits there.
branches.cn: 抬高的数：这个形容词属于指数，也属于未知数坐在指数位置的方程。

branches.en: THE FUNCTION: the exponential function, whether named in full or shortened to a bare noun.
branches.cn: 函数本身：无论说全称还是缩成一个光秃秃的名词，指的都是指数函数。

branches.en: UP AND DOWN: growth and decay are the same fixed-factor rule running forward or backward.
branches.cn: 上升与下降：增长与衰减是同一条固定倍数规则的正向与反向。

branches.en: MEASURING TIME: waiting times and smoothed forecasts borrow the shape of the decay curve.
branches.cn: 计量时间：等待时间与平滑预测都借用了衰减曲线的形状。

branches.en: TIME THAT EXPLODES: in computing the step count doubles with every added item.
branches.cn: 爆炸的时间：在计算里，每多一个数据，步数就翻倍。

intro.en: Exponential is an English noun plus a Latin adjective suffix, and both parts are still productive.
intro.cn: exponential 是一个英语名词加拉丁形容词后缀构成，两部分至今都能产。

core_image: 一本旧数表摊开，密密麻麻的数字排成纵列，每一列都在回答「要抬到几次」

sceneCN: 这里 logarithm 指「对数，即为得到某数需要把底数抬到的幂」（第 1 个义项：对数的定义）；句意为在计算器出现之前，学生通过查印刷数表里的对数来求乘积。图中可辨识物件：对数表、书页、指尖、铅笔。

pos.zh: 对数；对数值

senses.title: The power needed to reach a number
senses.definition: the exponent to which a base must be raised to produce a given number
senses.definitionCN: 为使底数得到某个给定数而必须把底数抬到的幂
senses.example: The logarithm answers the question of how many times the base must multiply itself.
senses.exampleCN: 对数回答的是底数必须自乘多少次这个问题。
senses.why: the word was coined from Greek logoi 'ratios' plus arithmos 'number': the ratio-number, the number that measures the ratio.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由希腊语 logoi「比」与 arithmos「数」合成：比数，即衡量比值的那个数。

senses.title: The common logarithm
senses.definition: a logarithm taken to base ten, written without an explicit base in many texts
senses.definitionCN: 以十为底的对数，许多教材中不写出底数
senses.example: The common logarithm of one thousand is three.
senses.exampleCN: 一千的常用对数是三。
senses.why: base ten matches the decimal system, so the ten-based logarithm became the everyday one in calculation.
senses.whyCN: 以十为底与十进制相合，因此十底对数成了计算中的日常对数。

senses.title: The natural logarithm
senses.definition: a logarithm taken to the natural constant, the base that makes growth and decay equations simplest
senses.definitionCN: 以自然常数为底的对数，这个底使增长与衰减的方程最简洁
senses.example: The natural logarithm turns multiplication of growth factors into addition.
senses.exampleCN: 自然对数把增长因子的相乘变成相加。
senses.why: calculus keeps choosing the base whose logarithm has the simplest slope, and that base is called natural for this reason.
senses.whyCN: 微积分总是选那个对数斜率最简单的底，这个底正因此被称为「自然」。

senses.title: The binary logarithm
senses.definition: a logarithm taken to base two, common in computing
senses.definitionCN: 以二为底的对数，常见于计算领域
senses.example: The binary logarithm of the number of leaves gives the depth of the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 叶子数量的二进制对数给出这棵树的深度。
senses.why: computer memory splits in two at every step, so base two measures its depth exactly.
senses.whyCN: 计算机存储每一步都一分为二，因此以二为底正好量出它的深度。

senses.title: A table of logarithms
senses.definition: a printed table listing logarithms so that products can be found by adding
senses.definitionCN: 印好的对数数值表，靠相加就能求出乘积
senses.example: The engineer carried a logarithm table in the same case as his slide rule.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把对数表和计算尺装在同一个盒子里。
senses.why: before machines, the table was the practical form of the idea: turn multiplication into addition and look it up.
senses.whyCN: 在没有机器的年代，数表就是这个想法的实用形态：把乘法变成加法再查表。

senses.title: A law of logarithms
senses.definition: a rule such as the logarithm of a product equals the sum of logarithms
senses.definitionCN: 诸如「积的对数等于对数的和」这样的规则
senses.example: The law of logarithms replaced a long multiplication with two short additions.
senses.exampleCN: 对数运算法则把一次很长的乘法换成两次短加法。
senses.why: the whole reason logarithms were invented is that they turn products into sums, which is exactly what the law states.
senses.whyCN: 对数被发明的全部理由就在于把积化为和，这条法则说的正是这件事。

senses.title: The logarithm as a function
senses.definition: the function that assigns to each positive number its logarithm
senses.definitionCN: 把每个正数对应到它的对数的函数
senses.example: The logarithm grows slowly, so it compresses huge ranges into a small interval.
senses.exampleCN: 对数函数增长缓慢，把巨大的范围压进一个小间隔。
senses.why: once the numerical value became a rule applied to every positive input, the logarithm was a function.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个数值变成对每个正输入都适用的规则，对数就成了一个函数。

senses.title: The discrete logarithm
senses.definition: the exponent that solves a power equation within a finite arithmetic system, used in cryptography
senses.definitionCN: 在有限算术系统中解出幂方程的指数，用于密码学
senses.example: The security of the protocol rests on how hard the discrete logarithm is to find.
senses.exampleCN: 这个协议的安全性取决于离散对数有多难求。
senses.why: cryptography took the ordinary logarithm and confined it to a finite system, where finding it becomes deliberately hard.
senses.whyCN: 密码学拿过普通对数，把它限制在有限系统中，找起来就变得刻意地困难。

senses.title: The complex logarithm
senses.definition: an extension of the logarithm to complex numbers, defined with an infinite family of values
senses.definitionCN: 把对数推广到复数，并用无穷多个值来定义
senses.example: The complex logarithm has infinitely many branches.
senses.exampleCN: 复对数有无限多个分支。
senses.why: extending the logarithm past zero forces a choice of branch, so the single value becomes a family.
senses.whyCN: 把对数越出零之外，就迫使人们选择分支，单个值于是变成一族值。

intro.en: Logarithm is a coined scientific term: Greek logos, here in the sense 'ratio', joined to arithmos 'number'. John Napier introduced it in 1614 to name the number that measures a ratio.
intro.cn: logarithm 是一个人造的科学术语：希腊语 logos 在此取「比」义，与 arithmos「数」结合。纳皮尔在 1614 年引入它，用来命名衡量比值的那个数。

items.en: Logos carried a wide range of meanings: word, account, reason and, in mathematics, ratio or proportion. The mathematical sense is the one used here.
items.cn: logos 的含义很广：言词、账目、理性，在数学里则指比或比例。这里用的是数学义。

items.en: Arithmos meant 'number'. Its earlier origin is not securely established, and any pre-Greek form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: arithmos 意为「数」。它更早的来源没有可靠定论，凡为其给出的前希腊语形式都属重构。

items.en: John Napier combined the two Greek elements to mean a number measuring a ratio, and published the new word in his description of the logarithmic tables.
items.cn: 纳皮尔把这两个希腊构件合起来，指「衡量比值的数」，并在他介绍对数表的著作中公布了这一新词。

items.en: The coinage was Latinized as logarithmus and passed into the European languages through scholarly Latin.
items.cn: 这个新造词被拉丁化为 logarithmus，再经学术拉丁语传入欧洲各语言。

items.en: English adopted logarithm in the seventeenth century together with the tables, and the shorter form log followed in usage.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪随对数表一起接受了 logarithm，更短的 log 随后也在使用中出现。

items.en: The coining and its date are documented, but the deeper origin of arithmos is source uncertain; the commonly repeated pre-Greek etymology is a reconstruction rather than a proven derivation.
items.cn: 造词与年代有文献可查，但 arithmos 的更早来源不确定；常被转述的前希腊语词源是重构形式，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds close to logarithm; the second group names the quantities and tools that sit beside it.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 logarithm 相近；第二组是与它相邻的量与工具。

entries.definition: The adjective of logarithm; it describes scales and curves, not the number itself.
entries.definitionCN: logarithm 的形容词，描述刻度与曲线，而非那个数本身。

entries.definition: From Greek arithmetike 'the art of counting', built on the same arithmos 'number'; it names the subject, not a ratio-measuring number.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 arithmetike「计数的技艺」，同样建立在 arithmos「数」上；它指这门学科，不是衡量比值的数。

entries.definition: From the name al-Khwarizmi through Medieval Latin; it looks like logarithm but has no Greek logos or arithmos inside.
entries.definitionCN: 经中世纪拉丁语来自花拉子米的名字；看似 logarithm，里面却没有希腊的 logos 或 arithmos。

entries.definition: From Greek logistikos 'skilled in calculation', but it developed separately to mean supply management and a growth model.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 logistikos「精于计算」，但独立发展出后勤管理与一种增长模型的意思。

entries.definition: The number whose logarithm is given; it reverses the lookup rather than performing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指对数为某值的那个数；它把查表反过来，而非执行查表。

entries.definition: The power itself; a logarithm is that power asked as a question about a result.
entries.definitionCN: 指幂本身；对数则是把这个幂当作「要得到某结果」的问题来问。

entries.definition: The result of repeated multiplication; the logarithm names the count of repetitions.
entries.definitionCN: 指重复相乘的结果；对数命名的则是重复的次数。

entries.definition: A relation between two amounts; the 'ratio' inside logarithm names what the number measures, not a quotient itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个量之间的关系；logarithm 里的「比」说明这个数衡量什么，而不是指商本身。

entries.definition: A calculating tool that works by adding lengths proportional to logarithms.
entries.definitionCN: 一种计算工具，靠相加与对数成比例的长度来运算。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek pieces, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Greek logos 'ratio' plus arithmos 'number': a ratio-number, the number that measures a ratio.
normal.cn: 希腊 logos「比」加 arithmos「数」：比数，衡量比值的那个数。

normal.en: The family runs logarithm, logarithmic, logarithmically and antilogarithm.
normal.cn: 同族词有 logarithm、logarithmic、logarithmically 与 antilogarithm。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the bases: common logarithm, natural logarithm, binary logarithm.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出底数：常用对数、自然对数、二进制对数。

normal.en: The whole point is stated in one line: the log of a product is the sum of the logs.
normal.cn: 全部要点可以写成一行：积的对数等于对数的和。

normal.en: Before machines, people turned multiplication into addition and then read the answer off a table.
normal.cn: 在没有机器的年代，人们把乘法变成加法，再从表上读出答案。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose steps get shorter and shorter but never quite end.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯，台阶越来越矮，却始终走不完。

abstract.en: Picture a giant compressed into a small box, still recognizable in outline.
abstract.cn: 想象一个巨人被压进小盒子，轮廓仍然认得出来。

abstract.en: Picture a question that asks not 'what is the answer' but 'how many times did you multiply'.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问题不问「答案是多少」，而问「你乘了几次」。

examples.en: The logarithm of a product equals the sum of the logarithms of its factors.
examples.cn: 积的对数等于各因子对数的和。

examples.en: Engineers once read logarithms from books the way we now read screens.
examples.cn: 工程师曾像我们今天读屏幕一样从书本上读对数。

examples.en: On a logarithmic scale the logarithm itself becomes the distance along the axis.
examples.cn: 在对数尺度上，对数本身就变成沿轴的这段距离。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「逻各」配「节奏」——按固定的「比例节奏」一层层数上去 → 对数

root: 希腊 logos（比、比例、言词）+ arithmos（数）→ 近代拉丁 logarithmus，纳皮尔 1614 年造词。arithmos 更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all ask the same question in different settings: how many times must the base be multiplied? The answer is read from a definition, a base, a table, a law, a function, a cipher or a complex branch.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项在不同场合问同一个问题：底数要乘多少次？答案分别从定义、底数、数表、法则、函数、密码系统或复分支中读出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old table of columns, each column answering the question 'raised how many times'.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本旧数表排着纵列，每一列都在回答「要抬到几次」。

branches.en: THE QUESTION ITSELF: the exponent needed to reach a given number.
branches.cn: 问题本身：为得到某个给定数所需的幂。

branches.en: THE CHOICE OF BASE: ten for decimals, the natural constant for calculus, two for machines.
branches.cn: 底数的选择：十进制用十，微积分用自然常数，机器用二。

branches.en: THE OLD TOOL: a printed table and the law that turns products into sums.
branches.cn: 旧工具：印好的数表，以及把积化为和的法则。

branches.en: THE FUNCTION: the same value applied to every positive input.
branches.cn: 函数：把同一个值应用到每个正输入上。

branches.en: BEYOND ORDINARY NUMBERS: a deliberately hard exponent in ciphers, and an infinite family of branches in the complex plane.
branches.cn: 越出普通数之外：密码中刻意难求的指数，以及复平面上无穷多个分支。

intro.en: Logarithm is a modern coinage from two Greek nouns, so its building blocks are combining forms rather than inherited prefixes and suffixes.
intro.cn: logarithm 是由两个希腊名词合成的近代新词，因此它的构件其实是组合形式，而非继承下来的前缀与后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Greek elements logos and arithmos entered Latin as logos and arithmus; the coinage logarithmus is modern Latin, not classical.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊构件 logos 与 arithmos 以 logos、arithmus 的形式进入拉丁语；logarithmus 是近代拉丁造词，不属于古典拉丁。

items.example: The first element contributes the idea of ratio.
items.exampleCN: 第一个构件贡献「比」这个意思。

items.example: The second element contributes the idea of number.
items.exampleCN: 第二个构件贡献「数」这个意思。

items.example: The logarithm measures how often the base is raised.
items.exampleCN: 对数衡量底数被抬了几次。

items.example: The scale is logarithmic.
items.exampleCN: 这个刻度是对数的。

items.example: The values grow logarithmically.
items.exampleCN: 这些数值按对数方式增长。

items.meaning: the number matching a given logarithm
items.example: The antilogarithm reverses the lookup.
items.exampleCN: 反对数把查表反过来。

items.example: Arithmetic uses the same number element.
items.exampleCN: 算术用的是同一个「数」构件。

items.meaning: logarithm in informal and technical use
items.example: The program takes the log of the input.
items.exampleCN: 程序对输入取对数。

core_image: 一根尺子上的刻度越往右越挤，每一格代表的倍数却一样大
scene: 图纸的横轴上，刻度越往右越密，每一格代表同样的倍数。The plotted points fall on a logarithmic scale that compresses the largest values.
sceneCN: 这里 logarithmic 指「按对数刻度的，即等长的一段代表相同的倍数」（第 2 个义项：对数尺度）；句意为这些点落在一条把最大值压缩了的对数刻度上。图中可辨识物件：坐标纸、不均匀的刻度、数据点、直尺。
