senses.title: Of or using logarithms
senses.definition: connected with logarithms or carried out by means of them
senses.definitionCN: 与对数有关，或借助对数来完成的
senses.example: The old calculation was done by a logarithmic method.
senses.exampleCN: 这项老式计算是用对数方法完成的。
senses.why: the adjective simply marks anything that belongs to or works through logarithms.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是标记任何属于对数、或经由对数运作的事物。

senses.title: On a logarithmic scale
senses.definition: arranged so that equal distances on the axis stand for equal ratios rather than equal amounts
senses.definitionCN: 安排成轴上等长的距离代表相同的比值，而非相同的数量
senses.example: The plotted points fall on a logarithmic scale that compresses the largest values.
senses.exampleCN: 这些点落在一条把最大值压缩了的对数刻度上。
senses.why: a log scale keeps the ratio visible while squeezing the range, which is why it can hold both tiny and huge values.
senses.whyCN: 对数刻度在压缩范围的同时保留了比值，因此能同时容纳极小与极大的值。

senses.title: Logarithmic in form
senses.definition: describing an equation or expression whose unknown appears inside a logarithm
senses.definitionCN: 描述未知数出现在对数内部的方程或表达式
senses.example: The logarithmic equation is solved by rewriting it in exponential form.
senses.exampleCN: 这个对数方程通过改写成指数形式来求解。
senses.why: the equation is named after the operation that encloses the unknown, not after the growth of its solution.
senses.whyCN: 这个方程以「把未知数包住的那个运算」命名，而不是以解的增长率命名。

senses.title: Logarithmic growth
senses.definition: growth that slows steadily, so each further increase requires a much larger input
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐放慢的增长，越往后每增加一点都需要大得多的投入
senses.example: Memory research showed logarithmic growth in recall as study time increased.
senses.exampleCN: 记忆研究显示，随着学习时间增加，回忆量呈对数增长。
senses.why: because the logarithm of a number rises slowly, a quantity that grows logarithmically looks like it is levelling off.
senses.whyCN: 因为一个数的对数上升缓慢，按对数增长的量看起来就像正在走平。

senses.title: The logarithmic decrement
senses.definition: the logarithm of the ratio between two successive amplitudes of a damped oscillation
senses.definitionCN: 阻尼振荡中相邻两次振幅之比的对数
senses.example: The logarithmic decrement measures how quickly the pendulum's swing dies away.
senses.exampleCN: 对数减量衡量摆的摆动衰减得多快。
senses.why: a damping ratio is naturally spoken of through its logarithm, so the measured quantity carries the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 阻尼比天然要用它的对数来说，因此这个测得的量带着这个形容词。

senses.title: Logarithmic differentiation
senses.definition: a calculus method that takes the logarithm of both sides before differentiating
senses.definitionCN: 先对两边取对数、再求导的微积分方法
senses.example: Logarithmic differentiation made the product of five factors manageable.
senses.exampleCN: 对数求导法让五个因子的乘积变得好处理。
senses.why: the method works because logarithms turn products into sums, so the adjective names the step that unlocks the derivative.
senses.whyCN: 这个方法之所以有效，是因为对数把积化成和，形容词命名的正是打开导数的那一步。

senses.title: The logarithmic spiral
senses.definition: a curve that grows outward by a constant factor with every turn
senses.definitionCN: 每转一圈就按固定倍数向外扩张的曲线
senses.example: The shell follows a logarithmic spiral, widening at a constant rate.
senses.exampleCN: 这只贝壳沿着对数螺旋生长，以恒定的比例变宽。
senses.why: the radius of this spiral is an exponential function of the angle, so its description inverts into a logarithm.
senses.whyCN: 这条螺旋的半径是角度的指数函数，因此用对数来描写它。

senses.title: Logarithmic graph paper
senses.definition: paper printed with logarithmic rulings so that ratios appear as equal distances
senses.definitionCN: 印有对数格线的纸，使比值表现为等长的距离
senses.example: The students plotted the data on logarithmic graph paper to see the straight line.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们把数据画在对数坐标纸上，好看出那条直线。
senses.why: the paper is the physical form of the scale: equal spacing stands for equal ratios.
senses.whyCN: 这种纸就是刻度的实物形态：等间距代表等比值。

senses.title: Logarithmic complexity
senses.definition: describing an algorithm whose work grows with the logarithm of the input size
senses.definitionCN: 描述工作量随输入规模的对数增长的算法
senses.example: A binary search has logarithmic complexity, so doubling the list adds only one step.
senses.exampleCN: 二分查找具有对数复杂度，列表翻倍只多一步。
senses.why: each step of a halving search removes half the input, so the step count tracks the logarithm of the size.
senses.whyCN: 折半查找每一步都去掉一半输入，因此步数跟着规模的对数走。

intro.en: Logarithmic is logarithm plus the Greek adjective suffix -ic, which reached English through Latin -icus. It appears with the spread of logarithmic tables in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: logarithmic 是 logarithm 加希腊形容词后缀 -ic 构成，后者经拉丁 -icus 进入英语。它随对数表在十七世纪的传播而出现。

items.en: The Greek suffix -ikos formed adjectives meaning 'of or belonging to'; it was borrowed into Latin as -icus.
items.cn: 希腊后缀 -ikos 构成意为「属于……的」形容词；它被借入拉丁语作 -icus。

items.en: Latin -icus passed through French into English as -ic, the ending seen in arithmetic, geometric and logarithmic.
items.cn: 拉丁 -icus 经法语进入英语作 -ic，arithmetic、geometric 与 logarithmic 用的都是这个结尾。

items.en: Napier's logarithm was Latinized as logarithmus, and European scholars quickly formed adjectives from it.
items.cn: 纳皮尔的对数被拉丁化为 logarithmus，欧洲学者很快由它造出形容词。

items.en: English logarithmic appears in the seventeenth century alongside the tables and the new methods of calculation.
items.cn: 英语 logarithmic 在十七世纪与对数表及新的计算方法一同出现。

items.en: In later centuries the adjective attached to scales, spirals, decrements and algorithms, all cases where a ratio is read as a distance.
items.cn: 在后来的几个世纪里，这个形容词附着到刻度、螺旋、减量与算法上，都是把比值读成距离的场合。

items.en: The first English citation for the adjective is approximate; the suffix history and the base coinage are documented.
items.cn: 这个形容词在英语中的最早书证为约数；后缀的历史与基词的造词过程则有文献可查。

note.en: The first group shares the logarithm stem or the -ic ending and is easily confused; the second group names related scales and shapes.
note.cn: 第一组共享 logarithm 词干或 -ic 词尾，容易混淆；第二组是相关的刻度与形状。

entries.definition: The number itself; the adjective describes anything built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指那个数本身；形容词则描述建立在它之上的事物。

entries.definition: The adverb, describing how something grows or is plotted rather than what it is.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，描述某物如何增长或如何作图，而非它是什么。

entries.definition: From logistikos 'skilled in calculation', but it names logistics and an S-shaped growth curve, not logarithms.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 logistikos「精于计算」，但指后勤学与一条先慢后快再趋缓的增长曲线，不是对数。

entries.definition: From logos in its 'reason' sense; it shares the Greek word but not the mathematical ratio sense used in logarithm.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 logos 的「理性」义；共享那个希腊词，但不共享 logarithm 所用的数学「比」义。

entries.definition: From the name al-Khwarizmi, not from logos or arithmos; it describes procedures, not scales.
entries.definitionCN: 来自花拉子米的名字，并非出自 logos 或 arithmos；描述的是过程，不是刻度。

entries.definition: Describes growth by a fixed factor; a logarithmic scale is the way that growth looks when flattened for viewing.
entries.definitionCN: 描述按固定倍数增长；对数刻度则是这种增长被压平后呈现的样子。

entries.definition: On a linear scale equal distances stand for equal amounts, the opposite of what a logarithmic scale does.
entries.definitionCN: 在线性刻度上等距离代表相等的量，与对数刻度的做法相反。

entries.definition: Squeezed into a smaller span; a logarithmic scale compresses a wide range, but the word itself says nothing about ratios.
entries.definitionCN: 被压进更小的跨度；对数刻度会压缩很宽的范围，但这个词本身不涉及比值。

entries.definition: Marked off in regular divisions; a scale can be graduated without being logarithmic.
entries.definitionCN: 按规则分度标出；一个刻度可以有分度却不是对数的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Logarithm plus -ic: the adjective of the ratio-number.
normal.cn: logarithm 加 -ic：比数这个词的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs logarithm, logarithmic, logarithmically and antilogarithm.
normal.cn: 同族词有 logarithm、logarithmic、logarithmically 与 antilogarithm。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: logarithmic scale, logarithmic spiral, logarithmic differentiation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：对数刻度、对数螺旋、对数求导法。

normal.en: On a log scale the small values get room and the giants get squeezed.
normal.cn: 在对数刻度上，小数值分到空间，巨无霸被挤扁。

normal.en: The -ic ending is the same one heard in arithmetic, geometric and chaotic.
normal.cn: 这个 -ic 词尾与 arithmetic、geometric、chaotic 里听到的是同一个。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose marks crowd together as the numbers grow, yet each gap still means the same ratio.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子，数字越大刻度越挤，可每一格仍然代表同样的比值。

abstract.en: Picture a spiral shell that widens by the same fraction at every turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一只螺旋贝壳，每转一圈就按同样的比例变宽。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase that adds one step for every doubling of the climb.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯，每把高度翻一倍，才加一级台阶。

examples.en: Earthquake strength is reported on a logarithmic scale.
examples.cn: 地震强度按对数刻度报告。

examples.en: The logarithmic spiral appears in shells, storms and galaxies.
examples.cn: 对数螺旋出现在贝壳、风暴与星系中。

examples.en: Binary search is logarithmic, so the list can double for one extra step.
examples.cn: 二分查找是对数级的，所以列表翻倍只多一步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「逻各节奏」的尺子——按比例的节奏一格一格量 → 对数的、对数刻度的

root: 英语 logarithm（对数，希腊 logos「比」+ arithmos「数」）+ 希腊—拉丁形容词后缀 -ic（-ikos / -icus）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses apply one measuring idea: equal steps stand for equal ratios. The idea appears as a method, a scale, an equation, a slow curve, a damping measure, a calculus trick, a spiral, ruled paper and an algorithm.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项应用同一个测量想法：等长的步子代表相同的比值。这个想法分别表现为方法、刻度、方程、缓慢曲线、阻尼量、微积分技巧、螺旋、格纸与算法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler whose marks crowd together on the right while each gap still means the same ratio.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子，右边的刻度挤在一起，而每一格仍代表相同的比值。

branches.en: THE MEASURE AND THE SCALE: anything done by logarithms, and the axis where equal steps mean equal ratios.
branches.cn: 测量与刻度：任何借对数完成的事，以及等步长代表等比值的那条轴。

branches.en: EQUATION AROUND A LOG: the unknown is wrapped inside the logarithm.
branches.cn: 包着对数的方程：未知数被裹在对数里面。

branches.en: SLOW RISE: the curve keeps climbing but each new unit costs much more input.
branches.cn: 缓慢上升：曲线仍在爬，但每一点新进展都要大得多的投入。

branches.en: DAMPING AND DERIVATIVES: a decrement read through a logarithm, and a derivative unlocked by taking one.
branches.cn: 阻尼与导数：用对数读出的减量，以及先取对数才打开的导数。

branches.en: SHAPES AND TOOLS: the spiral, the ruled paper and the halving search all turn ratios into visible distances or steps.
branches.cn: 形状与工具：螺旋、格纸与折半查找，都把比值变成可见的距离或步数。

intro.en: Logarithmic is a coined noun with a Greek adjective ending; the ending is old, the base is early modern.
intro.cn: logarithmic 是一个人造名词加希腊形容词词尾；词尾古老，基词则是近代早期的产物。

latinIntro.en: The Greek elements are logos and arithmos; Latin supplied the adjective ending -icus and the modern coinage logarithmus.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊构件是 logos 与 arithmos；拉丁语提供了形容词词尾 -icus 与近代造词 logarithmus。

items.example: It supplies the ratio half of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供这个词里「比」的那一半。

items.example: It supplies the number half of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供这个词里「数」的那一半。

items.example: The noun names the measure itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名那个量本身。

items.example: The scale is logarithmic.
items.exampleCN: 这个刻度是对数的。

items.example: The values rise logarithmically.
items.exampleCN: 这些值按对数上升。

items.example: The antilogarithm returns the original number.
items.exampleCN: 反对数还原出原来的数。

items.meaningCN: 表示归属的形容词后缀
items.example: It is the same ending as in arithmetic.
items.exampleCN: 它与 arithmetic 用的是同一个词尾。

items.example: The code takes the log of the value.
items.exampleCN: 代码对这个值取对数。

definition_zh: 分数；一小部分；极少量；馏分
definition_en: a number written as one quantity divided by another, or a small part of a whole
core_image: 一整块面包被切开，其中一片孤零零地留在盘子里
scene: 一块面包被切成同样大小的几片，盘子里只剩下一片。Only a fraction of the loaf was left on the plate.
sceneCN: 这里 fraction 指「整体中的一小部分」（第 2 个义项：不完整的一份）；句意为盘子里只剩下这块面包的一小部分。图中可辨识物件：面包、切片、空盘子、刀。

pos.zh: 分数；小部分；少量；馏分

derivatives.zh: 骨折；断裂（同出拉丁 frangere）

senses.title: A number written as a quotient
senses.definition: a number expressed as one integer divided by another, showing parts of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 用一个整数除以另一个整数来表示的数，显示整体的若干份
senses.example: Three quarters is a fraction that can also be written as a decimal.
senses.exampleCN: 四分之三是一个分数，也可以写成小数。
senses.why: fraction is Latin for 'a breaking': the whole is broken into equal pieces, and the written number records how many are taken.
senses.whyCN: fraction 在拉丁语里是「一次断裂」：整体被打成等份，写下来的数记录取走了几份。

senses.title: A part of a whole
senses.definition: a piece or share of something larger, not necessarily a mathematical number
senses.definitionCN: 较大事物中的一片或一份，不一定是数学意义上的数
senses.example: Only a fraction of the loaf was left on the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 盘子里只剩下这块面包的一小部分。
senses.why: the mathematical sense is only the most exact version of the older physical sense: a broken-off piece.
senses.whyCN: 数学义只是更早的实物义「掰下来的一块」最精确的版本。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: a tiny proportion of a cost, a difference or a quantity
senses.definitionCN: 成本、差额或数量中极小的一份
senses.example: The repair cost a fraction of what a new machine would cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修理只花了买新机器的一小部分钱。
senses.why: because a fraction can be as small as one part in a million, the word came to mean 'almost nothing' in comparison.
senses.whyCN: 因为分数可以小到百万分之一，这个词便引申为「相比之下几乎不算什么」。

senses.title: A very short moment
senses.definition: an extremely brief period of time
senses.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间
senses.example: The camera shutter stayed open for a fraction of a second.
senses.exampleCN: 相机快门只开了零点几秒。
senses.why: time is treated as a whole and cut into tiny pieces, so a sliver of a second is naturally a fraction of it.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当作一个整体切成小片，一秒钟的薄薄一片自然就是它的一小部分。

senses.title: A cut from distillation
senses.definition: one of the portions collected when a mixture is separated by boiling
senses.definitionCN: 混合物经沸腾分离时收集到的其中一份
senses.example: The lightest fraction of the crude oil leaves the column first.
senses.exampleCN: 原油中最轻的馏分最先离开分馏塔。
senses.why: distillation literally cuts a mixture into successive pieces, so chemistry reused the word for each cut.
senses.whyCN: 分馏字面上就是把混合物依次切成若干段，化学便用这个词指每一段。

senses.title: The written common fraction
senses.definition: a fraction written with one number above a line and another below it
senses.definitionCN: 一个数写在横线上方、另一个数写在横线下方的分数写法
senses.example: Write the common fraction with a bar between the two numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 把普通分数写成两个数中间加一道横线。
senses.why: the bar is the visible mark of the break, which is why this notation is called a common fraction.
senses.whyCN: 这道横线正是「断开」的可见标记，因此这种写法被称作普通分数。

senses.title: A breakaway group
senses.titleCN: 旧义：分裂出来的小派别
senses.definition: an older use for a small party or sect split off from a larger body
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指从较大团体中分裂出来的小派别
senses.example: A small fraction withdrew from the assembly and met apart.
senses.exampleCN: 一小派退出大会，另行集会。
senses.why: a group that breaks away is literally a broken piece of the larger body, so the older political sense kept the physical image.
senses.whyCN: 分裂出去的群体就是较大团体被掰下的一块，因此这个旧的政治义保留了实物的形象。

senses.title: The breaking of the bread
senses.definition: the ceremonial breaking of the eucharistic bread in some churches
senses.definitionCN: 某些教会仪式中把圣餐饼掰开的动作
senses.example: The congregation stood during the Fraction.
senses.exampleCN: 掰饼时会众站立。
senses.why: the rite is literally a breaking, so the Latin word for breaking survived as the name of that moment.
senses.whyCN: 这个仪式字面上就是一次掰开，于是那个表示「断裂」的拉丁词作为这一刻的名称留存下来。

senses.title: The fractional part of a mixed number
senses.definition: the part of a mixed number that is written as a proper fraction
senses.definitionCN: 带分数中以真分数形式写出的那一部分
senses.example: In the mixed number, the fraction is the part after the whole number.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个带分数里，分数部分是整数后面的那一段。
senses.why: a mixed number is a whole plus a broken remainder, and the remainder is named by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 带分数是一个整数加一段剩下的碎块，这段剩余就用同一个词命名。

intro.en: Fraction comes from Latin fractio 'a breaking', from frangere 'to break'. English took it through French, first as a general word for a broken piece and later as the arithmetic term.
intro.cn: fraction 来自拉丁 fractio「一次断裂」，出自 frangere「打破」。英语经法语引入，最初泛指掰下来的一块，后来才成为算术术语。

items.en: Frangere meant 'to break, shatter'. The same root gives fragile, fragment and fracture, and also refract, where light is broken back.
items.cn: frangere 意为「打破、击碎」。同一词根给出 fragile、fragment 与 fracture，也给出 refract，即把光折回去。

items.en: Fractio, from the participle fractus, named the act or result of breaking, hence a broken piece.
items.cn: fractio 出自分词 fractus，命名断裂的动作或结果，因此指掰下来的一块。

items.en: Old French fraccion carried the word into English in the fourteenth century with the sense of a fragment or a broken part.
items.cn: 古法语 fraccion 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，意思是碎片或断裂的部分。

items.en: The mathematical use, a number expressing parts of a unit, is recorded from the fifteenth century and became dominant with printed arithmetic books.
items.cn: 数学用法即表示单位若干份的数，从十五世纪起有记录，并随着印刷算术书普及而占据主导。

items.en: In the nineteenth century fraction was applied to the portions collected in distillation, a literal cutting of a mixture into pieces.
items.cn: 十九世纪时，fraction 被用于分馏中收集的各部分，字面上就是把混合物切成若干段。

items.en: The first dates for the arithmetic and chemical senses are approximate; the Latin etymon itself is secure.
items.cn: 算术义与化学义的最早年代都是约数；拉丁语源本身是可靠的。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for breaking and is easily confused; the second group names other shares and pieces.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「打破」的拉丁动词，容易混淆；第二组是其他表示份额与碎片的词。

entries.definition: A break in bone or rock; it keeps the literal sense of breaking, while fraction moved toward measured parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指骨头或岩石的断裂；保留「断」的字面义，而 fraction 转向了被量出的部分。

entries.definition: A piece broken off; it stresses the physical chip rather than the numerical relation.
entries.definitionCN: 指掰下来的碎片，强调实物碎块而非数值关系。

entries.definition: Easily broken; the adjective keeps the passive side of frangere.
entries.definitionCN: 指容易破碎，保留 frangere 被动的一面。

entries.definition: From Latin factio, built on facere 'to do'; it means a party or clique and has nothing to do with breaking.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 factio，建立在 facere「做」上；指党派或小集团，与「打破」无关。

entries.definition: From fricare 'to rub'; it looks like fraction but names resistance between surfaces, not a part of a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 fricare「摩擦」；形似 fraction，但指表面之间的阻力，不是整体的一部分。

entries.definition: Any portion of a whole; it carries no arithmetic value and no sense of breaking.
entries.definitionCN: 指整体的任何一部分，不含算术数值，也不含「断裂」的意思。

entries.definition: A share assigned to someone; it emphasizes distribution rather than the size of the piece.
entries.definitionCN: 指分给某人的一份，强调分配，而非那块的大小。

entries.definition: One person's part of something divided among several; fraction can be purely numerical.
entries.definitionCN: 指在若干人之间分给某人的那份；fraction 可以纯属数值。

entries.definition: A comparison of two quantities; a fraction can express a ratio but is itself a single number.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个量的比较；分数可以表示比值，但它本身是一个单数。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: frangere 'to break': a fraction is a piece broken off the whole.
normal.cn: frangere「打破」：分数就是从整体上掰下来的一块。

normal.en: The family runs fraction, fractional, fractionate, fractionation and fracture.
normal.cn: 同族词有 fraction、fractional、fractionate、fractionation 与 fracture。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday sense: a fraction of the cost, a fraction of a second.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出日常义：成本的一小部分、零点几秒。

normal.en: The bar in a fraction is the visible line where the whole was broken.
normal.cn: 分数里的那道横线，就是整体被掰断时留下的可见痕迹。

normal.en: Distillation cuts a mixture into fractions just as the arithmetic word cuts a unit into parts.
normal.cn: 分馏把混合物切成馏分，正如算术里的这个词把单位切成若干份。

abstract.en: Picture a plate with one slice left and the rest already eaten.
abstract.cn: 想象盘子里只剩一片，其余都已被吃掉。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler broken so that only a short splinter remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子断了，只剩下一小截薄片。

abstract.en: Picture a whole choir walking out of the hall in a small group.
abstract.cn: 想象整个合唱团里有一小群人走出大厅。

examples.en: Two thirds is a fraction larger than one half.
examples.cn: 三分之二是一个大于二分之一的分数。

examples.en: The machine can finish the job in a fraction of the time.
examples.cn: 这台机器能在很短的时间内完成这项工作。

examples.en: Each fraction from the distillation column has a different boiling range.
examples.cn: 分馏塔出来的每个馏分都有不同的沸程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗拉克」听起来像「裂开」——整块裂下一片 → 分数、一小部分

root: 拉丁 frangere「打破」→ fractio「一次断裂」→ 古法语 fraccion → 英语 fraction。同根有 fragile、fragment、fracture、refract。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all begin with one break: a whole is split, and what is left in the hand is the fraction, whether it is a number, a slice, a moment, a distilled cut, a splinter group or a broken loaf.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都始于同一次断裂：整体被劈开，手里剩下的那一块就是 fraction，无论它是一个数、一片面包、一瞬时间、一段馏分、一个分裂的小派别，还是一块掰开的面饼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a loaf cut into equal slices, with one slice alone on the plate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块面包被切成等份，盘子里只剩孤零零的一片。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN BREAK: the arithmetic number, the bar notation, and the remainder beside a whole number.
branches.cn: 写下来的断裂：算术的数、带横线的写法，以及整数旁边的那段余数。

branches.en: THE PIECE IN HAND: the oldest physical sense, a broken-off part of anything.
branches.cn: 手里的一块：最古老的实物义，任何东西掰下来的一部分。

branches.en: THE TINY SHARE: small enough to be almost nothing beside the whole.
branches.cn: 微小的一份：小到与整体相比几乎不算什么。

branches.en: A SLIVER OF TIME: the same cutting applied to a second.
branches.cn: 时间的一薄片：把同样的切法用在一秒上。

branches.en: BREAKING APART IN PRACTICE: a distilled cut, a splinter party and a broken loaf all keep the literal image.
branches.cn: 实际中的裂开：分馏的一段、分裂的小派别与掰开的面饼，都保留着字面上的形象。

intro.en: Fraction is a Latin noun of breaking with a productive suffix and a root that also builds several common English words.
intro.cn: fraction 是一个表示「断裂」的拉丁名词，带一个能产后缀，其词根还构成若干常见英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin frangere gives fraction, fracture, fragment, fragile and refract; the suffix -io, through French -ion, names the act or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 frangere 衍生 fraction、fracture、fragment、fragile 与 refract；后缀 -io 经法语 -ion，命名动作或其结果。

items.structure: frangere, fregi, fractum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The root supplies the act of breaking.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「打破」的动作。

items.example: The participle describes what has been broken.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词描述已经断掉的东西。

items.example: The noun names the break itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名断裂本身。

items.meaning: a broken piece; a number of parts
items.example: Only a fraction of the bread remained.
items.exampleCN: 只剩下一小部分面包。

items.example: The gain was fractional.
items.exampleCN: 这点增益微乎其微。

items.example: The plant fractionates the oil.
items.exampleCN: 工厂把原油分馏。

items.example: The fall caused a small fracture.
items.exampleCN: 这一摔造成一处小骨折。

items.example: A fragment of the vase was found.
items.exampleCN: 找到了花瓶的一块碎片。

items.example: The old paper is fragile.
items.exampleCN: 这种旧纸很脆。

derivatives.zh: 骨折；断裂（同出拉丁 frangere）

definition_zh: 十进制的；小数；小数位；十进制记数法
definition_en: based on the number ten, or a number written with a point to show parts smaller than one
core_image: 一把尺子每隔十格画一道粗线，格与格之间再分成十小格
scene: 收银台上，每张价签都在点后写着两位数字。Every price in the shop is written as a decimal with two places.
sceneCN: 这里 decimal 指「带小数点、表示不足一的部分的数」（第 2 个义项：小数）；句意为店里每张价签都写成保留两位的小数。图中可辨识物件：价签、收银机、商品、点后数字。

pos.zh: 十进制的；按十进位的
小数；带小数点的数

derivatives.zh: 大批杀死；严重削弱（同出拉丁 decem，但义为「取十分之一」）
十二进制的（同出拉丁 decem）

senses.title: Based on the number ten
senses.definition: organized in groups of ten, with each place worth ten times the one before
senses.definitionCN: 以十为一组组织，每一位的值是前一位的十倍
senses.example: The decimal system makes calculation with large numbers manageable.
senses.exampleCN: 十进制让大数计算变得好处理。
senses.why: decimal comes from Latin decimus 'tenth', and the whole system is built on the tenth step.
senses.whyCN: decimal 来自拉丁 decimus「第十」，整个系统正建立在「每十进一」上。

senses.title: A number with a point
senses.definition: a number written with a point to separate whole units from parts of a unit
senses.definitionCN: 用一个小点把整数单位与不足一的部分分开写出的数
senses.example: Every price in the shop is written as a decimal with two places.
senses.exampleCN: 店里每张价签都写成保留两位的小数。
senses.why: the point marks where the counting of whole units stops and the counting of tenths begins.
senses.whyCN: 这个小点标出整数单位数到哪里为止、十分位从哪里开始。

senses.title: A decimal place
senses.definition: one of the positions to the right of the decimal point, each worth a tenth of the one before
senses.definitionCN: 小数点右边的某一位，每一位是前一位的十分之一
senses.example: Rounding to one decimal place removed the noisy last digit.
senses.exampleCN: 保留一位小数就把最后那个嘈杂的数字去掉了。
senses.why: every step to the right divides by ten, so each position is literally a tenth part of the previous one.
senses.whyCN: 每往右一步就除以十，因此每一位确实是前一位的十分之一。

senses.title: Decimal notation
senses.definition: the written form of a number using digits and a point rather than a fraction bar
senses.definitionCN: 用数字与一个小点而不是分数横线写出的形式
senses.example: Decimal notation is easier to compare on a screen than stacked fractions.
senses.exampleCN: 在屏幕上，小数记法比上下叠写的分数更容易比较。
senses.why: the notation is named after the base it uses, because its places advance by powers of ten.
senses.whyCN: 这种记法以它所用的底数命名，因为它的数位按十的幂前进。

senses.title: Decimal currency
senses.definition: a money system in which each unit divides into a hundred or a thousand subunits
senses.definitionCN: 每个单位细分为一百或一千个次一级单位的货币制度
senses.example: Decimal currency replaced shillings and pence in many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 十进制货币在许多国家取代了先令与便士。
senses.why: money became decimal when the old non-ten divisions were dropped for tenths and hundredths.
senses.whyCN: 当旧的非十进位细分被十与百取代时，货币就成了十进制的。

senses.title: A repeating decimal
senses.definition: a decimal in which one or more digits repeat without end
senses.definitionCN: 一个或几个数字无限重复的小数
senses.example: One third written as a decimal is a repeating decimal.
senses.exampleCN: 三分之一写成小数是一个循环小数。
senses.why: some fractions never divide evenly by ten, so the decimal expansion repeats forever.
senses.whyCN: 有些分数永远除不尽十，因此小数展开会一直重复。

senses.title: A decimal fraction
senses.definition: a fraction whose denominator is a power of ten, usually written with a point
senses.definitionCN: 分母是十的幂、通常用一个小点写出的分数
senses.example: The decimal fraction is only another way of writing the same value.
senses.exampleCN: 十进制分数只是同一个值的另一种写法。
senses.why: when the denominator is a power of ten, the fraction can be written in place-value form and called decimal.
senses.whyCN: 当分母是十的幂时，分数就能用位值形式写出，因此被称为十进制的。

senses.title: Decimal classification
senses.definition: a library system that divides all knowledge into ten main classes, numbered from zero to nine
senses.definitionCN: 把所有知识分成十个大类、以零到九编号的图书分类体系
senses.example: The librarian found the book under its decimal classification.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆员按这本书的十进制分类号找到了它。
senses.why: the system is called decimal because every level of division uses ten branches.
senses.whyCN: 这套体系之所以称十进制，是因为每一层细分都用十个分支。

senses.title: Decimal degrees
senses.definition: an angle or coordinate expressed as a decimal rather than in minutes and seconds
senses.definitionCN: 用小数而不是分与秒表示的角度或坐标
senses.example: The map stores the position in decimal degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 地图以十进制度保存该位置。
senses.why: the degree is kept as a unit and its fractions are written in tenths instead of minutes, hence decimal.
senses.whyCN: 度数保留为单位，其零头改用十分位而不是分来写，因此是十进制的。

intro.en: Decimal comes from Latin decimus 'tenth', from decem 'ten', with the adjective ending -al. The mathematical use spread in the seventeenth century with decimal arithmetic.
intro.cn: decimal 来自拉丁 decimus「第十」，出自 decem「十」，并带形容词词尾 -al。数学用法随十进制算术在十七世纪传播开来。

items.en: Decem meant 'ten'. The Indo-European source is usually reconstructed with a form meaning 'ten', but the exact shape is a reconstruction rather than a recorded item.
items.cn: decem 意为「十」。其印欧语来源通常被重构为一个意为「十」的形式，但确切形态是重构，不是有记录的词项。

items.en: Decimus meant 'tenth', the ordinal built on decem; it names the position reached after nine steps.
items.cn: decimus 意为「第十」，是建立在 decem 上的序数词；它命名走完九步后到达的位置。

items.en: The adjective decimalis was formed in medieval Latin from decimus to describe reckoning by tenths.
items.cn: 形容词 decimalis 在中世纪拉丁语中由 decimus 构成，用来描述按十分位计算的方式。

items.en: Decimal entered English mathematical writing in the seventeenth century, when decimal fractions and the written point became common.
items.cn: decimal 在十七世纪进入英语数学文献，当时十进制小数与书写的小数点开始普及。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word was applied to money systems and to the library classification that divides knowledge into ten classes.
items.cn: 在十九、二十世纪，这个词被用于货币制度，也被用于把知识分成十个大类的图书分类法。

items.en: The precise first citation of each applied sense is approximate; decem and decimus are securely attested Latin words.
items.cn: 每个应用义的确切首见书证都是约数；decem 与 decimus 则是有可靠记录的拉丁词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin word for ten and is easily mistaken; the second group names other number systems and written forms.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「十」的拉丁词，容易误认；第二组是其他数制与书写形式。

entries.definition: Historically to kill one in ten as punishment; it shares decem but has nothing to do with place value.
entries.definitionCN: 历史上指为惩罚而十人中杀一；同样出自 decem，但与位值无关。

entries.definition: A period of ten years; it comes from Greek dekas 'a group of ten', a different but related counting word.
entries.definitionCN: 指十年；来自希腊 dekas「十人一组」，是不同但相关的计数词。

entries.definition: A unit built with the prefix deci- 'tenth' plus bel; it measures sound by a logarithmic ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「十分之一」的前缀加 bel 构成的单位，用对数比值衡量声音。

entries.definition: Built on duodecim 'twelve' with decem inside; it describes base twelve, not base ten.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁语中表示「十二」的词构成，里面含 decem；描述十二进制，而非十进制。

entries.definition: One tenth of a metre; the prefix deci- carries the tenth, while decimal describes the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 指十分之一米；前缀只带「十分之一」，而 decimal 描述整个体系。

entries.definition: A learned synonym for base-ten, built on Latin deni 'ten each'; it is rarer than decimal.
entries.definitionCN: 十进制的一个书面同义词，建立在拉丁语中表示「每十个」的词上；比 decimal 更少见。

entries.definition: Describing parts of a unit; it says nothing about whether the parts are counted in tenths.
entries.definitionCN: 描述单位的部分，并不说明这些部分是否按十分位计数。

entries.definition: A written symbol for a number; decimal names a system, while numeral names the mark.
entries.definitionCN: 指表示数的书写符号；前者命名体系，后者命名记号。

entries.definition: A measuring system whose units step by powers of ten; it is decimal in its design but not a synonym for every decimal number.
entries.definitionCN: 指按十的幂进位的度量体系；它在设计上是十进的，但不是所有小数的同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin word for ten, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「十」、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin decem 'ten': every place is worth ten times the one to its right.
normal.cn: 拉丁 decem「十」：每一位都是它右边那一位的十倍。

normal.en: The family runs decimal, decimalize, decimalization, decimally and duodecimal.
normal.cn: 同族词有 decimal、decimalize、decimalization、decimally 与 duodecimal。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: decimal point, decimal place, decimal currency.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：小数点、小数位、十进制货币。

normal.en: The point is a hinge: whole units on the left, tenths on the right.
normal.cn: 小数点是铰链：左边是整数单位，右边是十分位。

normal.en: A decimal fraction is simply a fraction whose denominator is a power of ten.
normal.cn: 十进制分数不过是分母为十的幂的分数。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase with ten steps to every landing, then ten more to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象每十级台阶到一个平台，再十级到下一个平台。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler that keeps halving the gap, but always by ten instead of two.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子不断把间隔细分，只是每次按十而不是按二。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag where the last two digits are the crumbs of a dollar.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签，最后两位数字是一块钱掉下的碎屑。

examples.en: The measurement was recorded to three decimal places.
examples.cn: 这个测量值记录到三位小数。

examples.en: The country changed to decimal currency in the nineteen sixties.
examples.cn: 这个国家在二十世纪六十年代改用十进制货币。

examples.en: Turning the fraction into a decimal made the comparison obvious.
examples.cn: 把分数化成小数后，比较就一目了然了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得西」——「十」的音——按十往下分，一位一位往右走 → 十进制的、小数

root: 拉丁 decem「十」→ decimus「第十」→ 中世纪拉丁 decimalis → 英语 decimal。印欧语「十」的形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all keep the tenth step: a system in tens, a number with a point, a place worth a tenth, a notation, a currency, a repeating tail, a fraction with a power of ten below, a library scheme and a coordinate.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都保留「每十进一」这一步：十进体系、带点的数、值是十分位的数位、记法、货币、循环的尾巴、分母为十的幂的分数、图书分类体系与坐标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler marked in tens, with each gap split again into ten.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把按十标度的尺子，每段间隔再细分成十小格。

branches.en: TEN AS THE UNIT: the base-ten system and the money that divides each unit into a hundred.
branches.cn: 以十为单位：十进体系，以及把每个单位细分成一百的货币。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN SPLIT: a point separates whole units from parts, and digits replace the fraction bar.
branches.cn: 写下来的分割：小点把整数单位与零头分开，数字取代了分数横线。

branches.en: TENTHS BELOW: each place is worth a tenth, and the denominator is a power of ten.
branches.cn: 往下的十分位：每一位值十分之一，分母则是十的幂。

branches.en: THE ENDLESS TAIL: a fraction that never divides evenly repeats its digits forever.
branches.cn: 无尽的尾巴：除不尽十的分数，其数字永远重复。

branches.en: TEN BRANCHES ELSEWHERE: libraries split knowledge into ten classes, and maps split a degree into tenths.
branches.cn: 别处的十个分支：图书馆把知识分成十大类，地图把一度细分成十分位。

intro.en: Decimal is a Latin ordinal turned adjective; its root is the common word for ten, and the endings are still productive.
intro.cn: decimal 是由拉丁序数词转成的形容词；其词根是「十」这个常用词，词尾至今能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin decem and decimus give decimal, decimate, decimeter and duodecimal; the ending -alis, through French -al, forms relational adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 decem 与 decimus 衍生 decimal、decimate、decimeter 与 duodecimal；词尾 -alis 经法语 -al 构成关系形容词。

items.example: The base of the whole system is ten.
items.exampleCN: 整个体系的底数是十。

items.example: The ordinal names the tenth step.
items.exampleCN: 这个序数命名第十步。

items.example: The medieval adjective described tenth-based reckoning.
items.exampleCN: 这个中世纪形容词描述以十为基的计算。

items.meaning: based on ten; a pointed number
items.example: The price is written as a decimal.
items.exampleCN: 价格写成小数。

items.meaning: to convert to a decimal system
items.example: The country decimalized its currency.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家把货币改为十进制。

items.example: Decimalization simplified the accounts.
items.exampleCN: 十进化让账目变简单了。

items.example: The scale is divided decimally.
items.exampleCN: 这个刻度按十进制划分。

items.meaningCN: 大批毁掉（原义为「十中取一」）
items.example: The storm decimated the orchard.
items.exampleCN: 风暴毁掉了果园的一大半。

items.example: It turns the noun of ten into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把「十」的名词变成形容词。

十二进制的（同出拉丁 decem）

definition_zh: 商；除法的结果；比率；商群、商环等代数结构；智商、情商等的简称
definition_en: the result of dividing one number by another, or a structure built by treating two things as equivalent
core_image: 一道除法竖式算完，横线上方写出一个得数

sceneCN: 这里 quotient 指「除法所得的结果」（第 1 个义项：商）；句意为减法完成后，商被写在除法横线的上方。图中可辨识物件：黑板、竖式、横线、写出的得数。

pos.zh: 商；除法结果；比率；（数学结构中的）商

senses.title: The result of a division
senses.definition: the number obtained when one quantity is divided by another
senses.definitionCN: 用一个量除以另一个量时得到的数
senses.example: The quotient is written above the division line after the subtraction.
senses.exampleCN: 减法完成后，商被写在除法横线的上方。
senses.why: Latin quotiens means 'how many times': the quotient answers how many times the divisor fits into the dividend.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 quotiens 意为「多少次」：商回答的就是除数在被除数里能放多少次。

senses.title: The whole-number quotient
senses.definition: the whole part of the result when a division leaves a remainder
senses.definitionCN: 除法留下余数时，结果中取整的那一部分
senses.example: Dividing seventeen by five gives a whole-number quotient of three.
senses.exampleCN: 十七除以五，整数商是三。
senses.why: everyday division asks only how many whole times the divisor fits, which is the oldest arithmetic sense.
senses.whyCN: 日常除法常常只问除数能完整放几次，这正是最古老的算术义。

senses.title: The quotient group
senses.definition: a group formed by treating elements that differ by a subgroup as equivalent
senses.definitionCN: 把相差一个子群的元素视为等价后形成的群
senses.example: The quotient group collapses the subgroup into a single identity.
senses.exampleCN: 商群把这个子群压成一个单位元。
senses.why: the construction divides the group by a subgroup, exactly as numbers are divided, so algebra reused the arithmetic name.
senses.whyCN: 这个构造用子群去「除」原群，和数被除一模一样，代数便沿用了算术的名字。

senses.title: The quotient ring
senses.definition: a ring built by declaring elements differing by an ideal to be equivalent
senses.definitionCN: 把相差一个理想的元素视为等价后形成的环
senses.example: The quotient ring has fewer elements but keeps the same operations.
senses.exampleCN: 商环的元素更少，却保留同样的运算。
senses.why: ring theory repeats the group construction with an ideal, and the same dividing name follows.
senses.whyCN: 环论用理想重复了群的构造，同一个表示「除」的名字也随之而来。

senses.title: The quotient space
senses.definition: a space formed by gluing together points that lie in the same equivalence class
senses.definitionCN: 把同属一个等价类的点粘合起来形成的空间
senses.example: The quotient space of the line by a lattice is a circle.
senses.exampleCN: 直线按一个格点群取商空间，得到一个圆。
senses.why: topology divides a space by a relation and calls the result a quotient, keeping the arithmetic metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 拓扑用一个关系去「除」一个空间，把结果称为商，保留算术的比喻。

senses.title: The intelligence quotient
senses.definition: a score comparing a person's test performance with the average for their age
senses.definitionCN: 把某人的测试表现与同龄人平均水平相比较所得的分数
senses.example: The intelligence quotient was once reported as a simple ratio of two ages.
senses.exampleCN: 智商最初被报告为两个年龄的简单比值。
senses.why: the original score was literally a quotient, mental age divided by chronological age, and the arithmetic name stuck.
senses.whyCN: 最初的分数确实是一个商，即智力年龄除以实际年龄，这个算术名字就留了下来。

senses.title: The emotional quotient
senses.definition: a measure of a person's ability to recognize and manage emotion
senses.definitionCN: 衡量一个人识别与管理情绪能力的指标
senses.example: The emotional quotient of the team rose after the training.
senses.exampleCN: 培训之后，团队的情商提高了。
senses.why: the pattern of intelligence quotient was copied for other measured capacities, so emotional quotient followed as a parallel coinage.
senses.whyCN: 智商这个模式被复制到其他可测能力上，情商便作为平行造词出现。

senses.title: The reaction quotient
senses.definition: a ratio of product concentrations to reactant concentrations at a given moment
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻产物浓度与反应物浓度之比
senses.example: Comparing the reaction quotient with the equilibrium constant tells the direction.
senses.exampleCN: 把反应商与平衡常数相比较，就能判断反应方向。
senses.why: chemistry divides the products by the reactants, and a quotient is exactly what that division produces.
senses.whyCN: 化学把产物除以反应物，而这样除出来的正是商。

senses.title: The quotient rule in calculus
senses.definition: the rule for differentiating a function written as one expression divided by another
senses.definitionCN: 对一个写成一式除以另一式的函数求导的法则
senses.example: The quotient rule handles the derivative of one function over another.
senses.exampleCN: 商法则处理一个函数除另一个函数的导数。
senses.why: the rule is named after the quotient it differentiates, not after the result it produces.
senses.whyCN: 这条法则以它所求导的那个商命名，而不是以它产生的结果命名。

intro.en: Quotient comes from Latin quotiens 'how many times', an adverb built on quot 'how many'. It entered English through French as the name of the division result.
intro.cn: quotient 来自拉丁 quotiens「多少次」，这是由 quot「多少」构成的副词。它经法语进入英语，成为除法结果的名称。

items.en: Quot was the interrogative word for 'how many', used in counting questions; it is the seed of the whole family.
items.cn: quot 是表示「多少」的疑问词，用于计数的提问；它是整个词族的种子。

items.en: Quotiens meant 'how many times' and was used in arithmetic to introduce the result of a division.
items.cn: quotiens 意为「多少次」，在算术中用来引出除法的结果。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed the noun quotientem from the adverb, naming the number that answers 'how many times'.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语由这个副词构成名词 quotientem，命名回答「多少次」的那个数。

items.en: French quotient carried the term into English in the Middle Ages, where it settled as the standard arithmetic word.
items.cn: 法语 quotient 在中世纪把这个术语带入英语，并在那里固定为标准算术词。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word was extended to algebraic structures such as quotient groups, and to measured capacities such as intelligence quotient.
items.cn: 在十九、二十世纪，这个词被扩展到商群这类代数结构，也被扩展到智商这类可测能力。

items.en: The first English citation and the exact date of the medieval noun formation are approximate; quot and quotiens are securely attested.
items.cn: 英语最早书证与中世纪名词构词的确切年代都是约数；quot 与 quotiens 则有可靠记录。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin 'how many' stem and is easy to mix up; the second group names division results and related quantities.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁「多少」这个词干，容易混淆；第二组是除法结果及相关量。

entries.definition: From Latin quota pars 'what part', a fixed share assigned; it is a portion, not a division result.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 quota pars「哪一份」，指分配定的份额；是一份配额，不是除法结果。

entries.definition: From quotare 'to mark with numbers, cite', originally to number chapters; it now means to repeat words or name a price.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 quotare「标上数目、引章节」，原指给章节编号；现在指引述原话或报价。

entries.definition: The noun of quote: a cited passage or a stated price, never a result of division.
entries.definitionCN: quote 的名词：引文或报出的价格，绝不是除法结果。

entries.definition: From quotidie 'daily', built on quot plus dies 'day'; it means everyday, not divided.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 quotidie「每日」，由 quot 加 dies「日」构成；意为日常的，与除法无关。

entries.definition: A relation between two quantities; a quotient is the single number that results from dividing them.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个量之间的关系；商则是把它们相除后得到的那个单数。

entries.definition: The outcome of any operation; quotient is specific to division.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何运算的结果；quotient 专指除法。

entries.definition: The quantity being divided, the input rather than the quotient.
entries.definitionCN: 指被除的那个量，是输入而不是商。

entries.definition: The number by which the dividend is divided; the quotient is the answer.
entries.definitionCN: 指用来除的那个数；商则是答案。

entries.definition: A division written as a top and bottom number; its value equals the quotient of the two.
entries.definitionCN: 写成上下两数的除法；它的值等于两数相除的商。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin interrogative, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁疑问词、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin quot 'how many' plus the time-ending: the quotient answers 'how many times'.
normal.cn: 拉丁 quot「多少」加时间词尾：商回答的就是「多少次」。

normal.en: The family runs quotient, quota, quote and quotation, all from the counting stem.
normal.cn: 同族词有 quotient、quota、quote 与 quotation，都出自那个计数词干。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modern uses: quotient group, reaction quotient, intelligence quotient.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出现代用法：商群、反应商、智商。

normal.en: A quotient is what remains after the divisor has fitted as many times as it can.
normal.cn: 商就是除数尽量放完若干次之后剩下的那个数。

normal.en: Every 'quotient' in higher mathematics is a division in disguise.
normal.cn: 高等数学里的每一个「商」，都是一次改头换面的除法。

abstract.en: Picture a box being filled by a smaller scoop, and the count of scoops is the quotient.
abstract.cn: 想象用一个小勺往箱子里装，装了多少勺就是商。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd sorted into equal rows, with the number of rows left over as the answer.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人排成等长的行，排成的行数就是答案。

abstract.en: Picture a score that compares your age with your ability, written as one number over another.
abstract.cn: 想象一个分数，把你的能力与年龄相比，写成一数除以另一数。

examples.en: The quotient of twelve divided by four is three.
examples.cn: 十二除以四的商是三。

examples.en: The reaction quotient tells which way the reaction will shift.
examples.cn: 反应商说明反应会往哪个方向移动。

examples.en: The quotient group is smaller, but its structure still reflects the original.
examples.cn: 商群更小，但它的结构仍反映原来的群。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阔申」——除完之后「阔」出来的一份 → 商

root: 拉丁 quot「多少」→ quotiens「多少次」→ 中世纪拉丁名词 quotientem → 法语 quotient → 英语 quotient。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all answer one question: how many times does this fit into that? Arithmetic, algebra, topology, chemistry, psychology and calculus each ask it in their own way.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都在回答同一个问题：这个东西能放进那个东西几次？算术、代数、拓扑、化学、心理学与微积分各用自己的方式发问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long division finished, with one number written above the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道除法竖式算完，横线上方写着一个数。

branches.en: THE ANSWER AND THE WHOLE PART: the division result, and the integer left when a remainder remains.
branches.cn: 答案与整数部分：除法的结果，以及留下余数时取整的那一段。

branches.en: STRUCTURES BY DIVISION: groups, rings and spaces are all built by treating a substructure as nothing.
branches.cn: 用除法造结构：群、环与空间都是靠把一个子结构当作「无」来构造。

branches.en: MEASURED MIND: intelligence and emotion are both scored as a ratio against an average.
branches.cn: 被量化的心智：智商与情商都被写成相对于平均值的比值。

branches.en: CHEMICAL RATIO: products divided by reactants at a chosen moment.
branches.cn: 化学比值：在某一时刻把产物除以反应物。

branches.en: RULE FOR A RATIO: the derivative rule named after the quotient it handles.
branches.cn: 处理商的法则：以它所处理的那个商命名的求导法则。

intro.en: Quotient is built from a Latin question word and a noun ending; the same question word also built quota and quote.
intro.cn: quotient 由一个拉丁疑问词与一个名词词尾构成；同一个疑问词还造出了 quota 与 quote。

latinIntro.en: Latin quot 'how many' gives quotiens 'how many times', quota 'what part', and quotare 'to number'; the English family keeps the counting idea throughout.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 quot「多少」衍生 quotiens「多少次」、quota「哪一份」与 quotare「编号」；英语词族始终保留计数的意思。

items.example: The question word starts the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个疑问词开启了整个词族。

items.example: The adverb asks the division question directly.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词直接提出了除法的问题。

definition_zh: 分子；分数线上方的数；除法中的被除数；比率中的前项
definition_en: the number above the line in a fraction, or the quantity that is divided by another
core_image: 一张纸上写着分数，横线上方的数字被红笔描了一道
scene: 纸上写着一个分数，横线上方的数字被红笔描了一道。In the fraction, the numerator tells how many parts are counted.
sceneCN: 这里 numerator 指「分数中写在横线上方的数，表示取了多少份」（第 1 个义项：分数的分子）；句意为在这个分数里，分子说明数了几份。图中可辨识物件：纸、分数横线、红笔、上下两个数字。

pos.zh: 分子；被除数；比的前项

senses.title: The number above the fraction bar
senses.definition: the number in a fraction that shows how many equal parts are taken
senses.definitionCN: 分数中说明取了多少个等份的那个数
senses.example: In the fraction, the numerator tells how many parts are counted.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个分数里，分子说明数了几份。
senses.why: numerator is Latin for 'counter': the top number counts the parts that the fraction is talking about.
senses.whyCN: numerator 在拉丁语里是「数数者」：上面那个数负责清点这个分数所说的份数。

senses.title: The dividend in a division
senses.definition: the quantity that is divided by another quantity
senses.definitionCN: 被另一个量所除的那个量
senses.example: In the written division, the numerator sits inside the bracket.
senses.exampleCN: 在竖式除法里，被除数写在除号里面。
senses.why: a fraction is a division written down, so the top number plays exactly the role of the dividend.
senses.whyCN: 分数就是写下来的除法，因此上面那个数扮演的正是被除数的角色。

senses.title: The first term of a ratio
senses.definition: the first quantity named when two amounts are compared as a ratio
senses.definitionCN: 两个量作比时先说出的那个量
senses.example: In the ratio, the numerator is the part being compared to the whole.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个比里，前项是被拿去与整体比较的那一部分。
senses.why: a ratio is a fraction in words, so the first term takes the place of the top number.
senses.whyCN: 比就是用文字说出的分数，因此前项占据的就是上面那个数的位置。

senses.title: The count in a rate
senses.titleCN: 比率中实际计数的部分
senses.definition: the number of events counted in the top part of a rate or proportion
senses.definitionCN: 比率或比例中，上半部分实际数出的事件数
senses.example: The numerator of the infection rate is the number of new cases.
senses.exampleCN: 感染率的分子是新病例的数目。
senses.why: in public health a rate is written as events over population, and the events are literally the counted numerator.
senses.whyCN: 在公共卫生里，率写成「事件数除以人口数」，事件数就是被数出来的分子。

senses.title: The numerator polynomial
senses.titleCN: 代数分式的分子多项式
senses.definition: the polynomial written above the line in an algebraic fraction
senses.definitionCN: 代数分式中写在横线上方的那个多项式
senses.example: Factor the numerator polynomial before simplifying the expression.
senses.exampleCN: 化简表达式之前，先把分子多项式因式分解。
senses.why: algebraic fractions copy ordinary fractions exactly, so the top polynomial keeps the name of the top number.
senses.whyCN: 代数分式完全照搬普通分数，因此上面那个多项式沿用上面那个数的名字。

senses.title: A common numerator
senses.definition: a numerator shared by two or more fractions after they are adjusted for comparison
senses.definitionCN: 两个或更多分数在调整以便比较后所共有的分子
senses.example: Rewriting both fractions with a common numerator made the larger one obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 把两个分数都改写成相同的分子后，较大的那个就一目了然了。
senses.why: just as fractions can share a denominator, they can be rewritten to share a numerator, and the counting role gives the name.
senses.whyCN: 正如分数可以有公分母，它们也能改写成共同的分子，命名依据仍是「数份」这个角色。

senses.title: The numerator of a percentage
senses.definition: the amount placed over one hundred when a proportion is written as a percentage
senses.definitionCN: 把比例写成百分数时，放在一百上面的那个量
senses.example: In the percentage, the numerator is the share and the denominator is one hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 在百分数里，分子是所占的份额，分母是一百。
senses.why: a percentage is a fraction with one hundred underneath, so the share above the line is still the numerator.
senses.whyCN: 百分数就是分母为一百的分数，因此横线上方的份额仍然是分子。

senses.title: An older word for a counter
senses.definition: an older use for a person who numbers or counts things
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指给事物编号或清点事物的人
senses.example: The old ledger lists the numerator who checked each crate.
senses.exampleCN: 旧账本上记着负责清点每个木箱的人。
senses.why: the Latin agent noun meant 'one who counts', and the mathematical use grew out of that literal counting person.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁施动名词本意是「数数的人」，数学用法正是从那个字面意义上的清点者长出来的。

intro.en: Numerator is Latin numerator 'a counter', from numerare 'to count', from numerus 'number'. The mathematical use came through French numérateur in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: numerator 是拉丁 numerator「数数者」，出自 numerare「计数」，再上溯到 numerus「数」。数学用法在十六世纪经法语 numérateur 而来。

items.en: Numerus meant 'number'. It is the source of numeral, numerical, enumerate and numerous in English.
items.cn: numerus 意为「数」。它是英语 numeral、numerical、enumerate 与 numerous 的来源。

items.en: Numerare meant 'to count, to number', a verb built directly on the noun.
items.cn: numerare 意为「计数、编号」，是直接由这个名词构成的动词。

items.en: The agent noun numerator named one who counts, a teller or reckoner; the ending -tor marks the person who does the action.
items.cn: 施动名词 numerator 指数数的人，即点算员；词尾 -tor 标记执行动作的人。

items.en: French formed the mathematical term numérateur for the top number of a fraction, since that number counts the parts taken.
items.cn: 法语构成数学术语 numérateur，指分数上方那个数，因为那个数负责清点取走的份数。

items.en: English adopted numerator in the sixteenth century together with the printed notation of fractions.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪随印刷的分数写法一起接受了 numerator。

items.en: The first English citation for the mathematical sense is approximate; numerus and numerare are securely attested Latin words.
items.cn: 数学义在英语中的最早书证为约数；numerus 与 numerare 则是有可靠记录的拉丁词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin word for number and is easily mixed up; the second group names the other parts of a division or ratio.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「数」的拉丁词，容易混淆；第二组是除法或比里的其他部分。

entries.definition: A written sign for a number; it names the mark, not the top part of a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指表示数的书写符号；命名的是记号，不是分数的上半部分。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning expressed in numbers; it describes data, not a fraction position.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「用数字表示的」，描述数据，不指分数的位置。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning able to handle numbers, or a verb meaning to count; neither is the fraction term.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词意为「会算数的」，动词意为「计数」；两者都不是分数术语。

entries.definition: To list one by one, from enumerare 'to count out'; it is a verb of listing, not a part of a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐项列出，出自 enumerare「数出来」；是列举的动词，不是分数的部分。

entries.definition: The bottom number, built on nomen 'name'; it names the size of the parts while the numerator counts them.
entries.definitionCN: 下面那个数，建立在 nomen「名字」上；它命名每份的大小，而分子负责数份数。

entries.definition: The quantity being divided; in a fraction it is the number above the bar.
entries.definitionCN: 指被除的量；在分数里就是横线上方的数。

entries.definition: The first term of a ratio, matching the numerator's position in a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指比的前项，对应分子在分数里的位置。

entries.definition: The number reached by counting; a numerator is that count written above a fraction bar.
entries.definitionCN: 指清点得到的数目；分子就是写成分数横线上方的那个清点结果。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for the numerator used in early teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 早期教学里对分子的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: numerus 'number' plus -ator 'one who': the counter, the number that counts the parts.
normal.cn: numerus「数」加 -ator「做……的人」：数数者，负责清点份数的那个数。

normal.en: The family runs numerator, numeral, numerical, numerate and enumerate, all from numerus.
normal.cn: 同族词有 numerator、numeral、numerical、numerate 与 enumerate，都出自 numerus。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: numerator and denominator, common numerator, numerator polynomial.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：分子与分母、公分子、分子多项式。

normal.en: The numerator sits on top and counts; the denominator sits below and names.
normal.cn: 分子在上面负责数，分母在下面负责命名。

normal.en: A percentage is just a fraction with one hundred below, so its top is still a numerator.
normal.cn: 百分数就是分母为一百的分数，所以它的上方仍然是分子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand picking up three slices from a loaf cut into eight.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从切成八片的面包里拿起三片。

abstract.en: Picture a tally keeper standing at the door, marking every person who enters.
abstract.cn: 想象一个记数人站在门口，给每个进来的人画一道。

abstract.en: Picture the number on top of a fraction as a small flag marking how much is claimed.
abstract.cn: 想象分数上面的数是面小旗，标出「要了多少」。

examples.en: When the numerator and denominator share a factor, both can be divided by it.
examples.cn: 分子与分母有公因子时，两边都能被它除。

examples.en: The numerator of the rate counts only confirmed cases.
examples.cn: 这个比率的分子只统计确诊病例。

examples.en: Write the numerator above the bar and the denominator below it.
examples.cn: 把分子写在横线上方，分母写在下方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「数在上」——负责点数的那一行写在上头 → 分子

root: 拉丁 numerus「数」→ numerare「计数」→ numerator「数数者」→ 法语 numérateur（分数上方的数）→ 英语 numerator。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep one role: the number that counts what is being taken. It counts slices of a fraction, items in a dividend, the first term of a ratio, cases in a rate, terms of a polynomial and parts of a percentage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个角色：负责清点「取走多少」的那个数。它数分数的份数、被除数里的个数、比的前项、比率中的病例、多项式的项，以及百分数里的份额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the number written above the fraction bar, marked with red ink.
core.cn: 核心意象：写在分数横线上方的数，被红笔描过。

branches.en: THE COUNTING POSITION: the top number of a fraction, and the shared top number used for comparison.
branches.cn: 计数的位置：分数的上方数，以及用于比较的公分子。

branches.en: THE SAME ROLE ELSEWHERE: the dividend of a division and the first term of a ratio.
branches.cn: 同一角色在别处：除法的被除数与比的前项。

branches.en: COUNTING WHAT HAPPENED: cases in a rate and the share written over one hundred.
branches.cn: 清点发生的事：比率中的病例，以及写在一百上面的份额。

branches.en: POLYNOMIAL ON TOP: algebraic fractions keep the top polynomial in the same seat.
branches.cn: 上面的多项式：代数分式让上方多项式坐同一个位置。

branches.en: THE PERSON WHO COUNTS: the oldest sense, the reckoner with a tally.
branches.cn: 数数的人：最古老的义项，拿筹码清点的人。

intro.en: Numerator is a Latin agent noun on a counting verb; its root and suffix both build a large English family.
intro.cn: numerator 是建立在一个计数动词上的拉丁施动名词；其词根与后缀都构成一个很大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin numerus gives numeral, numerical, numerous and enumerate; the agent suffix -tor gives numerator, denominator and operator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 numerus 衍生 numeral、numerical、numerous 与 enumerate；施动后缀 -tor 衍生 numerator、denominator 与 operator。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名被数的数。

senses.title: The number below the fraction bar
senses.definition: the number in a fraction that names the size of each equal part
senses.definitionCN: 分数中给每个等份的大小命名的那个数
senses.example: The denominator names the size of each part in the fraction.
senses.exampleCN: 分母给这个分数里每一份的大小命名。
senses.why: denominator is Latin for 'namer': the bottom number names what kind of part is being counted, thirds or fifths.
senses.whyCN: denominator 在拉丁语里是「命名者」：下面那个数命名被数的是几分之几。

senses.title: The divisor in a division
senses.definition: the quantity by which another quantity is divided
senses.definitionCN: 用来去除另一个量的那个量
senses.example: In the long division, the denominator stands outside the bracket.
senses.exampleCN: 在竖式除法里，除数写在除号外面。
senses.why: a fraction is a division written down, so the bottom number plays exactly the role of the divisor.
senses.whyCN: 分数就是写下来的除法，因此下面那个数扮演的正是除数的角色。

senses.title: The second term of a ratio
senses.definition: the second quantity named when two amounts are compared as a ratio
senses.definitionCN: 两个量作比时后说出的那个量
senses.example: In the ratio, the denominator is the whole to which the part is compared.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个比里，后项是被拿去比较的那一整个。
senses.why: a ratio is a fraction put into words, so the second term takes the seat of the bottom number.
senses.whyCN: 比就是用文字说出的分数，因此后项坐的就是下面那个数的位置。

senses.title: A common denominator as a shared basis
senses.titleCN: 引申义：共同点、共同基础
senses.definition: a feature shared by different things that makes them comparable
senses.definitionCN: 不同事物共有、使它们可以相互比较的特征
senses.example: A love of cheap travel was the common denominator of the group.
senses.exampleCN: 喜欢便宜的旅行是这个群体的共同点。
senses.why: fractions can only be added when they share a denominator, so the shared bottom number became a metaphor for shared ground.
senses.whyCN: 分数只有在分母相同时才能相加，于是共同的下面那个数成了「共同基础」的比喻。

senses.title: The least common denominator
senses.definition: the smallest number that can serve as the denominator of two or more fractions
senses.definitionCN: 能同时作为两个或更多分数分母的最小那个数
senses.example: Finding the least common denominator made the addition simple.
senses.exampleCN: 找到最小公分母让加法变简单了。
senses.why: the smallest shared bottom number is the practical choice when fractions must be combined, so it has its own fixed name.
senses.whyCN: 分数必须合并时，最小的共同下面那个数就是实用选择，因此它有自己的固定名称。

senses.title: The population at risk in a rate
senses.definition: the total number of people or items over which an event count is divided
senses.definitionCN: 用来除事件计数的那个总人数或总物件数
senses.example: The denominator of the death rate is the whole population at risk.
senses.exampleCN: 死亡率的分母是处在风险中的全部人口。
senses.why: a rate is events over population, and the population below the line is literally the denominator.
senses.whyCN: 率就是事件数除以人口数，写在横线下方的人口就是字面意义上的分母。

senses.title: The denominator polynomial
senses.titleCN: 代数分式的分母多项式
senses.definition: the polynomial written below the line in an algebraic fraction
senses.definitionCN: 代数分式中写在横线下方的那个多项式
senses.example: A zero of the denominator polynomial leaves the expression without a value.
senses.exampleCN: 分母多项式的零点会让表达式没有可取的值。
senses.why: algebraic fractions copy ordinary fractions, so the bottom polynomial keeps the name of the bottom number.
senses.whyCN: 代数分式照搬普通分数，因此下面那个多项式沿用下面那个数的名字。

senses.title: Rationalizing the denominator
senses.definition: the operation of removing a root or irrational number from the bottom of a fraction
senses.definitionCN: 把根号或无理数从分数下方去掉的运算
senses.example: Rationalizing the denominator made the exact value easier to read.
senses.exampleCN: 有理化分母后，精确值更容易读出来。
senses.why: the operation is named after the part it cleans, the denominator at the bottom of the fraction.
senses.whyCN: 这个运算以它清理的那一部分命名，也就是分数下方的分母。

senses.title: An older word for a namer
senses.definition: an older use for a person or thing that gives a name
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指给事物定名的人或物
senses.example: In the old text, the denominator of each district was the clerk who named it.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧文献里，每个辖区的命名者就是给它定名的书记。
senses.why: Latin denominare meant 'to name', and the agent noun kept that literal sense long before fractions adopted it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 denominare 意为「命名」，这个施动名词在分数借用它之前很久就保留着这个字面义。

intro.en: Denominator comes from Latin denominare 'to name', built on de- plus nomen 'name'. The fraction sense arrives through French dénominateur, because the bottom number names the kind of part.
intro.cn: denominator 来自拉丁 denominare「命名」，由 de- 加 nomen「名字」构成。分数义经法语 dénominateur 而来，因为下面那个数为「哪一种份」命名。

items.en: Nomen meant 'name'. It is the source of nominal, nomination, misnomer and the nomen in denominator.
items.cn: nomen 意为「名字」。它是 nominal、nomination、misnomer 的来源，也是 denominator 里的那个 nomen。

items.en: Nominare meant 'to name, call', a verb formed on nomen; its compounds name things in many directions.
items.cn: nominare 意为「命名、称呼」，由 nomen 构成的动词；它的复合形式向多个方向给事物命名。

items.en: De- plus nominare gave denominare 'to name, designate', with the prefix adding completion or specification.
items.cn: de- 加 nominare 构成 denominare「命名、指称」，前缀增添「彻底、具体化」的意思。

items.en: French formed dénominateur for the bottom number of a fraction, since that number names what size the parts are.
items.cn: 法语构成 dénominateur，指分数下面那个数，因为这个数命名每份的大小。

items.en: English adopted denominator in the sixteenth century, and the figurative 'common denominator' followed as fractions became everyday knowledge.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪接受了 denominator，随着分数成为常识，比喻义的「共同点」也随后出现。

items.en: The exact first citation for the figurative sense is approximate; nomen and nominare are securely attested Latin words.
items.cn: 比喻义的最早确切书证为约数；nomen 与 nominare 则是有可靠记录的拉丁词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin word for name and is easy to confuse; the second group names the other parts of a division or ratio.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「名字」的拉丁词，容易混淆；第二组是除法或比里的其他部分。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give a name or express in a unit; it is an action, not the bottom number.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为命名或以某单位表示；是动作，不是下面那个数。

entries.definition: A name, a religious body, or a unit value of money; it never means the bottom of a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指名称、教派或货币面额；从不指分数的下方。

entries.definition: In name only, or stated rather than real; it keeps nomen without the de- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指名义上的或标称的；保留 nomen 但没有那个表示「离开」的前缀。

entries.definition: A wrong or unsuitable name; it is built on nomen and names a naming error, not a fraction part.
entries.definitionCN: 指错误或不恰当的名称；由 nomen 构成，命名的是命名错误，不是分数的部分。

entries.definition: The top number, built on numerus 'number'; it counts parts while the denominator names them.
entries.definitionCN: 上面那个数，建立在 numerus「数」上；它负责数份数，而分母负责命名。

entries.definition: The number by which another is divided; in a fraction it is the number below the bar.
entries.definitionCN: 指用来除的那个数；在分数里就是横线下方的数。

entries.definition: The second term of a ratio, matching the denominator's position.
entries.definitionCN: 指比的后项，对应分母的位置。

entries.definition: A foundation or starting value; a common denominator is a figurative base for comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 指基础或起始值；公分母是用于比较的比喻性基础。

entries.definition: A standard used to judge; a common denominator is a shared feature, not a rule of judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 指用于判断的标准；公分母是共有特征，不是判断规则。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root and suffix, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根与后缀、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: nomen 'name' plus de- plus -ator: the namer at the bottom tells you what kind of part it is.
normal.cn: nomen「名字」加 de- 与 -ator：下面那个命名者告诉你这是几分之几。

normal.en: The family runs denominator, denominate, denomination, nominal and misnomer, all from nomen.
normal.cn: 同族词有 denominator、denominate、denomination、nominal 与 misnomer，都出自 nomen。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: common denominator, least common denominator, rationalize the denominator.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：公分母、最小公分母、有理化分母。

normal.en: The denominator names; the numerator counts. Name below, count above.
normal.cn: 分母负责命名，分子负责数数：名字在下，数在上。

normal.en: Two fractions can only be added when their denominators agree, which is why shared ground is called common.
normal.cn: 两个分数只有分母一致才能相加，这就是「共同基础」被称作「公」的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a knife cutting a cake into equal slices and writing the slice size on each one.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刀把蛋糕切成等份，并在每一片上写出这一份的大小。

abstract.en: Picture a room full of strangers who all discover they speak the same language.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子陌生人忽然发现彼此说同一种语言。

abstract.en: Picture a group of people counted against the whole town, with the town written below the line.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人被拿去与整个镇子相比，镇子的数目写在横线下方。

examples.en: A fraction with zero as its denominator is not defined.
examples.cn: 分母为零的分数没有定义。

examples.en: The two groups were compared on a common denominator of income.
examples.cn: 这两个群体按收入的共同基础来比较。

examples.en: Rationalizing the denominator removed the root from the bottom.
examples.cn: 有理化分母把根号从下方去掉了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得名」——下面那个数给整块「定名」，说明是几分之几 → 分母

root: 拉丁 nomen「名字」→ nominare「命名」→ denominare「定名」→ 法语 dénominateur（分数下方的命名者）→ 英语 denominator。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all keep one role: the number or feature that names the size of the parts. It names parts of a fraction, the divisor, the second term of a ratio, a shared basis, a population base, a polynomial and a cleaned root.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都保留同一个角色：为「每一份有多大」命名的那一个数或特征。它命名分数的份、除数、比的后项、共同基础、人口基数、多项式，以及被清理掉的根号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the number below the fraction bar, circled in blue like a label on each slice.
core.cn: 核心意象：分数横线下方的数，被蓝笔圈住，像每一份上的规格标签。

branches.en: THE NAMING NUMBER: the bottom number tells you the size of each part.
branches.cn: 命名的数：下面那个数告诉你每一份有多大。

branches.en: THE SAME ROLE ELSEWHERE: the divisor of a division and the second term of a ratio.
branches.cn: 同一角色在别处：除法的除数与比的后项。

branches.en: SHARED GROUND: a common bottom number, and the smallest one that two fractions can share.
branches.cn: 共同基础：共同的下面数，以及两个分数能共用的最小那个。

branches.en: WHAT THE LINE DIVIDES BY: the population at risk in a rate, and the polynomial below an algebraic fraction.
branches.cn: 横线用来除什么：比率中的风险人口，以及代数分式下方那个多项式。

branches.en: CLEANING AND NAMING: rationalizing removes a root from the bottom, while the oldest sense is a person who names.
branches.cn: 清理与命名：有理化把根号从下方去掉，而最古老的义项是给人定名的人。

intro.en: Denominator is a Latin agent noun on a verb of naming; its root, prefix and suffix all build English words.
intro.cn: denominator 是建立在「命名」动词上的拉丁施动名词；其词根、前缀与后缀都构成英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nomen gives nominal, nomination, misnomer and denomination; the prefix de- and the agent ending -tor complete the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nomen 衍生 nominal、nomination、misnomer 与 denomination；前缀 de- 与施动词尾 -tor 补全了这个词。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供命名的动作。

items.example: The verb turns the name into an act.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把名字变成动作。

items.example: The prefix makes the naming specific.
items.exampleCN: 前缀让命名变得具体。

items.meaning: one who names; the naming number

items.exampleCN: 分母命名每份的大小。

items.example: The unit was denominated in grams.
items.exampleCN: 这个单位以克来定名。

items.meaning: a name; a religious body; a money value
items.example: The notes come in several denominations.
items.exampleCN: 这些纸币有几种面额。

items.exampleCN: 名义费用只是一枚硬币。

items.exampleCN: 这个名字起得不对。

items.example: It also forms numerator and operator.

definition_zh: 乘法；成倍增加；增殖；繁殖；乘法运算
definition_en: the arithmetic operation of adding a number to itself a given number of times, or a large increase in number
core_image: 同样的几堆积木一排排摆开，堆数与每堆的块数交错相乘
scene: 课桌上摆开三排同样多的积木，孩子一排排数。The teacher introduces multiplication as repeated addition of equal groups.
sceneCN: 这里 multiplication 指「把若干相同数量的组相加的运算」（第 1 个义项：算术乘法）；句意为老师把乘法讲成相同组的重复相加。图中可辨识物件：积木、三排、课桌、孩子的手。

pos.zh: 乘法；增殖；繁殖；成倍增加

senses.title: The arithmetic operation
senses.definition: the operation of combining equal groups, or of adding a number to itself repeatedly
senses.definitionCN: 把若干相同数量的组合起来的运算，或把一个数重复相加
senses.example: The teacher introduces multiplication as repeated addition of equal groups.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把乘法讲成相同组的重复相加。
senses.why: multiplication is a folding of many equal copies into one total, which is exactly what the Latin root says.
senses.whyCN: 乘法就是把许多相同的副本叠合成一个总数，这正是拉丁词根说的意思。

senses.title: A large increase in number
senses.definition: a rapid or repeated increase in the number of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的数量迅速或反复地增加
senses.example: The multiplication of small shops changed the old market street.
senses.exampleCN: 小店铺的成倍增加改变了那条老市场街。
senses.why: the arithmetic operation reuses the same image outside arithmetic: many copies of one thing appear at once.
senses.whyCN: 算术运算把同一个形象用到算外：同一件东西一下子冒出许多副本。

senses.title: Cell multiplication
senses.definition: the process by which cells divide and increase in number
senses.definitionCN: 细胞分裂、数量增多的过程
senses.example: Uncontrolled cell multiplication is the mark of a tumour.
senses.exampleCN: 不受控制的细胞增殖是肿瘤的标志。
senses.why: biology describes tissues growing by copies, and the arithmetic word for copying fits the process exactly.
senses.whyCN: 生物学描述组织靠副本增长，而算术里表示「复制叠加」的词正合这个过程。

senses.title: Reproduction of animals
senses.definition: the increase of a population by breeding
senses.definitionCN: 种群通过繁育而数量增多
senses.example: The multiplication of the herd surprised the ranchers.
senses.exampleCN: 牛群的繁殖速度让牧场主吃惊。
senses.why: when animals breed, their numbers fold upward, so the older word for increase became a word for breeding.
senses.whyCN: 动物繁育时数量层层上翻，于是那个表示「增多」的老词成了繁育的词。

senses.title: The multiplication table
senses.definition: a printed grid of products of small numbers used for learning
senses.definitionCN: 印成网格、供学习使用的小数目乘积表
senses.example: She recited the multiplication table from memory.
senses.exampleCN: 她凭记忆背出了乘法表。
senses.why: the table is the operation written out in full, so it carries the name of the operation itself.
senses.whyCN: 乘法表就是把运算全部写出来，因此它带着运算本身的名字。

senses.title: Matrix multiplication
senses.definition: the rule for combining two arrays of numbers by summing products of rows and columns
senses.definitionCN: 把两个数字阵列按行与列的乘积求和来合并的规则
senses.example: Matrix multiplication is not commutative, so order matters.
senses.exampleCN: 矩阵乘法不满足交换律，所以顺序要紧。
senses.why: the operation sums products, which is a generalized multiplication of many terms at once.
senses.whyCN: 这个运算把许多乘积加起来，等于一次对许多项做推广的乘法。

senses.title: The multiplication sign
senses.definition: the symbol placed between numbers to show that they are multiplied
senses.definitionCN: 写在两个数之间、表示相乘的符号
senses.example: The multiplication sign was changed to a dot in the printed formula.
senses.exampleCN: 在印刷的公式里，乘号被改成了一个小点。
senses.why: the written sign is the operation made visible, so it is named after the operation.
senses.whyCN: 这个书写符号是运算的可见形式，因此以运算命名。

senses.title: The combined effect of several causes
senses.definition: the way separate efforts or causes reinforce one another
senses.definitionCN: 各自分开的努力或原因相互增强的方式
senses.example: The multiplication of small savings made the plan affordable.
senses.exampleCN: 一笔笔小节省叠加起来，让这个计划负担得起。
senses.why: effects that reinforce one another combine like equal groups, so the word for multiplying serves as a metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 相互增强的效果像相同的组一样合并，于是「相乘」这个词成了比喻。

senses.title: Logical multiplication
senses.definition: the Boolean operation that gives true only when every input is true
senses.definitionCN: 只有当所有输入都为真时才给出真的布尔运算
senses.example: Logical multiplication corresponds to the word and.
senses.exampleCN: 逻辑乘法对应的是「与」这个词。
senses.why: Boolean algebra borrows the arithmetic name because true and false combine in a strict table, like factors in a product.
senses.whyCN: 布尔代数借用算术名称，因为真假按严格的表组合，像乘积里的因子。

intro.en: Multiplication is Latin multiplicatio 'a multiplying', from multiplicare, built on multiplex 'many-fold', itself multus 'many' plus -plex 'fold'. English took it through French.
intro.cn: multiplication 是拉丁 multiplicatio「使增多」，出自 multiplicare，而后者建立在 multiplex「多重的」上，即 multus「多」加 -plex「折叠」。英语经法语引入。

items.en: Multus meant 'many, much'. It supplies the first half of the word and also appears in multiple and multitude.
items.cn: multus 意为「多」。它提供这个词的前半部分，也出现在 multiple 与 multitude 里。

items.en: Plicare meant 'to fold'. The same verb gives complicate, explicit, duplicate and multiply, all images of folding layers together.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」。同一个动词给出 complicate、explicit、duplicate 与 multiply，都是把层叠起来的形象。

items.en: Multus plus -plex produced multiplex 'many-fold, manifold', the adjective behind the whole family.
items.cn: multus 加 -plex 产生 multiplex「多重的、层叠的」，这是整个词族背后的形容词。

items.en: The verb multiplicare meant 'to make many-fold, to increase', and arithmetic narrowed it to the operation of repeated addition.
items.cn: 动词 multiplicare 意为「使成多重、使增多」，算术把它收窄为重复相加的运算。

items.en: Old French multiplication brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first in arithmetic and later in biology.
items.cn: 古法语 multiplication 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，先用于算术，后来用于生物学。

items.en: The first English date for the biological sense is approximate; the Latin pieces and the arithmetic sense are well documented.
items.cn: 生物学义的最早英语年代为约数；拉丁构件与算术义则有充分文献记录。

note.en: The first group shares the folding root and is easily confused; the second group names growth and reproduction.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「折叠」的词根，容易混淆；第二组是增长与繁殖的说法。

entries.definition: The verb of the operation; multiplication is the noun naming the act or the result.
entries.definitionCN: 运算的动词；multiplication 则是命名动作或结果的名词。

entries.definition: A number that another number divides exactly, or an adjective meaning many; it is not the operation.
entries.definitionCN: 指能被另一个数整除的数，或形容词「多个的」；不是运算本身。

entries.definition: The quality of being many; it counts kinds or instances, not products.
entries.definitionCN: 指「多」的性质；数的是种类或实例，不是乘积。

entries.definition: From explicare 'to unfold'; it means fully stated, and shares plicare without any arithmetic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 explicare「展开」；意为明确说出的，共享 plicare 但没有算术义。

entries.definition: From duo plus plicare, 'folded twice'; it means an exact copy, not a multiplication.
entries.definitionCN: 由 duo 加 plicare 构成，意为「折两次」；指完全相同的副本，不是乘法。

entries.definition: Any growth in size or number; multiplication suggests growth by copies or factors.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指大小或数量的增长；multiplication 暗示按副本或倍数增长。

entries.definition: A rapid increase in number, especially of cells or weapons; it stresses spread rather than the arithmetic rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指数量迅速增多，尤指细胞或武器；强调扩散而非算术规则。

entries.definition: The process by which living things produce offspring; multiplication can name the resulting increase.
entries.definitionCN: 指生物产生后代的过程；multiplication 可以指由此产生的数量增长。

entries.definition: Growth in size or scope; it does not imply equal groups or repeated addition.
entries.definitionCN: 指规模或范围的扩大；不含相同组或重复相加的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: multus 'many' plus plicare 'fold': many layers folded into one total.
normal.cn: multus「多」加 plicare「折」：许多层叠成一个总数。

normal.en: The family runs multiply, multiple, multiplicity, multiplication and multiplicative.
normal.cn: 同族词有 multiply、multiple、multiplicity、multiplication 与 multiplicative。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: multiplication table, matrix multiplication, multiplication sign.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：乘法表、矩阵乘法、乘号。

normal.en: Repeated addition of equal groups is the whole secret of the operation.
normal.cn: 相同组的重复相加，就是这项运算的全部秘密。

normal.en: Plicare also folds complicate, explicit and duplicate, so the family is all about layers.
normal.cn: plicare 还折出 complicate、explicit 与 duplicate，这个词族全都关于层叠。

abstract.en: Picture three trays, each holding four eggs, and the count arriving all at once.
abstract.cn: 想象三个托盘，每盘四个蛋，总数一下子就算出来了。

abstract.en: Picture a choir where every singer brings a friend, and the rows double.
abstract.cn: 想象合唱团里每个歌手都带来一个朋友，排数就翻倍了。

abstract.en: Picture one small saving repeated in many places until it becomes a large sum.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔小节省在许多地方重复出现，最后变成一大笔钱。

examples.en: Multiplication is commutative, so the order of the factors does not change the product.
examples.cn: 乘法满足交换律，因子的顺序不改变乘积。

examples.en: The multiplication of algae turned the pond green within a week.
examples.cn: 藻类的成倍繁殖让池塘一周内变绿。

examples.en: Matrix multiplication must be done in the stated order.
examples.cn: 矩阵乘法必须按规定的顺序进行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「满多」——相同的组越叠越多 → 乘法、成倍增加

root: 拉丁 multus「多」+ plicare「折叠」→ multiplex「多重的」→ multiplicare「使增多」→ multiplicatio → 古法语 → 英语 multiplication。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all fold equal copies together: the arithmetic operation, a manyfold rise, cells and herds, the printed table, matrices, the written sign, combined effects and a logical conjunction.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都把相同的副本叠在一起：算术运算、成倍上升、细胞与畜群、印好的表、矩阵、写下的符号、叠加的效果，以及逻辑上的合取。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: equal stacks of blocks laid in rows, counted by row times blocks.
core.cn: 核心意象：同样多的积木堆成几排，用排数乘每堆块数来数。

branches.en: THE OPERATION AND ITS TABLE: repeated addition, and the grid that writes it all out.
branches.cn: 运算与它的表：重复相加，以及把它全部写出的网格。

branches.en: MANYFOLD RISE: a rapid increase in number, and separate efforts reinforcing one another.
branches.cn: 成倍上升：数量的快速增多，以及分开的努力相互增强。

branches.en: LIFE MULTIPLYING: cells dividing and herds breeding, both growth by copies.
branches.cn: 生命在增殖：细胞分裂与畜群繁育，都是靠副本增长。

branches.en: FOLDING IN ROWS: matrix products and the written sign that marks the operation.
branches.cn: 按行折叠：矩阵的乘积，以及标记这项运算的书写符号。

branches.en: LOGICAL AND: true only when every factor is true, like a product that vanishes when any factor is zero.
branches.cn: 逻辑上的「与」：只有每个因子都真才为真，如同任何因子为零则乘积为零。

intro.en: Multiplication is a Latin action noun built from 'many' and 'fold'; both pieces and the suffix build a large family.
intro.cn: multiplication 是由「多」与「折叠」构成的拉丁动作名词；两个构件与后缀都构成一个很大的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin multus and plicare give multiple, multiplex, multiply, explicit, complicate and duplicate; the suffix -io, through French -ion, names the action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 multus 与 plicare 衍生 multiple、multiplex、multiply、explicit、complicate 与 duplicate；后缀 -io 经法语 -ion 命名动作或结果。

items.exampleCN: 第一个构件提供「多」。

items.example: The second element supplies the folding.
items.exampleCN: 第二个构件提供「折叠」。

items.example: The adjective describes many layers.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述许多层。

items.example: The verb is the act of folding many together.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是把许多层叠起来的动作。

items.example: The noun names the operation.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名这项运算。

items.example: Multiply the length by the width.

items.meaning: a number that divides another exactly
items.example: Twelve is a multiple of three.
items.exampleCN: 十二是三的倍数。

items.example: The multiplicity of options confused them.
items.exampleCN: 选项的繁多让他们困惑。

items.example: The instructions were explicit.
items.exampleCN: 说明写得很明确。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: It turns the verb of multiplying into the name of the act.
items.exampleCN: 它把「乘」的动词变成这项动作的名称。
