core_image: 两堆积木一层层往上叠，层数越高，块数翻得越快
scene: 两个孩子把积木一层层往上叠，越叠越高。If you multiply the side length by three, the area grows ninefold.
sceneCN: 这里 multiply 指「做乘法，把某个量乘上另一个量」（第 1 个义项：乘）；句意为把边长乘以三，面积就增大到九倍。图中可辨识物件：积木、两层堆叠、孩子的手、量尺。

pos.zh: 乘；使成倍增加
增多；繁殖；增殖

senses.title: To perform multiplication
senses.definition: to find the product of two or more numbers
senses.definitionCN: 求两个或更多数的乘积
senses.example: If you multiply the side length by three, the area grows ninefold.
senses.exampleCN: 把边长乘以三，面积就增大到九倍。
senses.why: multiply is the verb of folding equal copies together, and arithmetic uses it for the operation that counts those copies.
senses.whyCN: multiply 是把相同副本叠合起来的动词，算术用它来指清点这些副本的运算。

senses.title: To increase greatly
senses.definition: to make something much larger in number or amount
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物的数量或数额大大增加
senses.example: The new road multiplied the number of visitors ten times over.
senses.exampleCN: 新修的公路让访客数量增加了十倍。
senses.why: outside arithmetic the verb keeps the picture of many copies appearing: one cause produces a crowd of results.
senses.whyCN: 在算术之外，这个动词保留「许多副本出现」的画面：一个原因产生一大群结果。

senses.title: To grow in number
senses.definition: to become more numerous without an outside agent
senses.definitionCN: 在没有外来施动者的情况下变得更多
senses.example: Problems multiplied while the team was away.
senses.exampleCN: 团队不在的时候，问题越来越多。
senses.why: the intransitive use shifts the focus from someone making more to things simply becoming many.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法把焦点从「有人使变多」转到「事物自己变多」。

senses.title: To breed
senses.definition: to produce offspring and so increase a population
senses.definitionCN: 产生后代，从而使种群数量增加
senses.example: The rabbits multiplied faster than the gardeners could catch them.
senses.exampleCN: 兔子繁殖得比园丁抓得还快。
senses.why: breeding is increase by copies of living things, so the old verb for increase became the verb for breeding.
senses.whyCN: 繁育就是活物靠副本增多，于是那个表示「增多」的老动词成了繁育的动词。

senses.title: For cells to divide and increase
senses.definition: to increase in number by cell division
senses.definitionCN: 通过细胞分裂而数量增多
senses.example: The cells multiply until the wound is covered.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞不断增殖，直到伤口被覆盖。
senses.why: cell division repeats copies at a microscopic scale, and the arithmetic verb describes that repetition exactly.
senses.whyCN: 细胞分裂在微观尺度上重复副本，算术里的这个动词正描述这种重复。

senses.title: To multiply out
senses.definition: to expand a product of bracketed expressions by multiplying every term
senses.definitionCN: 把括号表达式的乘积逐项相乘展开
senses.example: Multiply out the brackets before collecting like terms.
senses.exampleCN: 先把括号乘开，再合并同类项。
senses.why: the particle 'out' marks the unfolding of a folded product, the reverse of the folding image inside the word.
senses.whyCN: 「乘开」里的「开」正标出把折起的乘积展开，与词内「折叠」的形象相反。

senses.title: To multiply by a number
senses.definition: to apply a particular factor to a quantity
senses.definitionCN: 对某个量施加一个特定的倍数
senses.example: Multiply the reading by ten to get the true value.
senses.exampleCN: 把读数乘以十，就得到真实值。
senses.why: this is the everyday phrasing of the operation, with the factor named after the preposition by.
senses.whyCN: 这是这项运算的日常说法，倍数在介词之后点出来。

senses.title: To multiply one's chances
senses.definition: to make an opportunity or risk much more likely
senses.definitionCN: 使某个机会或风险的可能性大大增加
senses.example: Two applications multiplied her chances of being accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 投出两份申请，让她被录取的机会成倍增加。
senses.why: chances behave like countable copies, so making more of them feels like multiplication rather than simple addition.
senses.whyCN: 机会像可数的副本，把机会变多感觉像相乘而不是简单相加。

intro.en: Multiply comes from Latin multiplicare 'to make many-fold', from multiplex, built on multus 'many' and plicare 'to fold'. English took the verb through Old French multiplier.
intro.cn: multiply 来自拉丁 multiplicare「使成多重」，出自 multiplex，由 multus「多」与 plicare「折叠」构成。英语经古法语 multiplier 引入这个动词。

items.en: Multus meant 'many'. It also lies behind multiple, multitude and the first half of multiply.
items.cn: multus 意为「多」。它也是 multiple、multitude 以及 multiply 前半部分的来源。

items.en: Plicare meant 'to fold'; the same verb gives explicit 'unfolded', complicate 'folded together' and duplicate 'folded twice'.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」；同一个动词给出 explicit「展开的」、complicate「折在一起」与 duplicate「折两次」。

items.en: Multus plus -plex made multiplex 'many-fold'; the adjective pictures layers folded onto one another.
items.cn: multus 加 -plex 构成 multiplex「多重的」；这个形容词描画一层层叠在一起。

items.en: The verb multiplicare meant 'to make many-fold, increase', and arithmetic narrowed it to repeated addition.
items.cn: 动词 multiplicare 意为「使成多重、使增多」，算术把它收窄为重复相加。

items.en: Old French multiplier carried the verb into English in the thirteenth century, first as 'increase' and then as the arithmetic operation.
items.cn: 古法语 multiplier 在十三世纪把这个动词带入英语，先表示「增多」，后表示算术运算。

items.en: The first English date for the arithmetic sense is approximate; the Latin verb and its parts are securely attested.
items.cn: 算术义在英语中的最早年代为约数；这个拉丁动词及其构件则有可靠记录。

note.en: The first group shares the folding root and is easily confused; the second group names other kinds of growth.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「折叠」的词根，容易混淆；第二组是其他增长方式。

entries.definition: A number divisible by another, or an adjective meaning many; it names a result, not the act of multiplying.
entries.definitionCN: 指能被另一个数整除的数，或形容词「多个的」；命名的是结果，不是相乘的动作。

entries.definition: The noun of the operation; it names the act or the process that multiply performs.
entries.definitionCN: 这项运算的名词；命名 multiply 所执行的动作或过程。

entries.definition: The quality of being many; it counts kinds or instances rather than performing a product.
entries.definitionCN: 指「多」的性质；数的是种类或实例，不做乘积。

entries.definition: Many-fold or having many parts; it keeps the old adjective without becoming a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指多重的或有许多部分的；保留老形容词，并未变成动词。

entries.definition: From explicare 'to unfold'; it shares plicare and means fully stated, with no arithmetic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 explicare「展开」；共享 plicare，意为明确说出的，没有算术义。

entries.definition: To become larger or more; it lacks the sense of equal copies folded together.
entries.definitionCN: 指变大或变多；不含相同副本叠合的意思。

entries.definition: To increase quickly by producing new parts; it stresses spreading, not the arithmetic rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过产生新部分而迅速增多；强调扩散，而非算术规则。

entries.definition: To produce offspring; multiplying can describe the resulting rise in numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生后代；multiplying 可以描述由此带来的数量上升。

entries.definition: To grow in size or scope; it does not imply counting equal groups.
entries.definitionCN: 指规模或范围扩大；不含清点相同组的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: multus 'many' plus plicare 'fold': to fold many copies into one product.
normal.cn: multus「多」加 plicare「折」：把许多副本折成一个乘积。

normal.en: The family runs multiply, multiplication, multiple, multiplicity and multiplier.
normal.cn: 同族词有 multiply、multiplication、multiple、multiplicity 与 multiplier。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: multiply by, multiply out, multiply in number.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：乘以、乘开、数量增多。

normal.en: Multiply out is the reverse of the folding inside the word: layers come apart into terms.
normal.cn: multiply out 与词内的「折」相反：层叠散开成为一项一项。

normal.en: Rabbits are the classic example of the breeding sense: they multiply faster than anyone can count.
normal.cn: 兔子是繁殖义的经典例子：它们增多得比谁数得都快。

abstract.en: Picture one brick that becomes two, then four, then eight, in the same minute.
abstract.cn: 想象一块砖在同一分钟里变成两块、四块、八块。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour spreading from one table to every table in the hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻从一桌传到大厅里的每一桌。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of brackets opening outward like a pair of hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一对括号像两只手一样向外张开。

examples.en: Multiply the length by the width to get the area.
examples.cn: 把长乘以宽就得到面积。

examples.en: Bacteria multiply rapidly in warm, moist conditions.
examples.cn: 细菌在温暖潮湿的条件下迅速繁殖。

examples.en: Multiply out the brackets and then simplify the result.
examples.cn: 把括号乘开，然后化简结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「满多倍」——一层层叠成多倍 → 乘、成倍增多

root: 拉丁 multus「多」+ plicare「折叠」→ multiplex「多重的」→ multiplicare「使增多」→ 古法语 multiplier → 英语 multiply。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one verb of folding copies: making a product, making much more, becoming many, breeding, cells dividing, opening brackets, applying a factor and swelling one's chances.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个「把副本叠起来」的动词：求乘积、使多得多、自身变多、繁殖、细胞分裂、打开括号、施加倍数，以及把机会撑大。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two stacks of blocks folded upward, the count rising faster than the height.
core.cn: 核心意象：两堆积木层层往上叠，块数比高度涨得更快。

branches.en: THE OPERATION: finding a product, and applying a named factor to a quantity.
branches.cn: 运算：求乘积，以及对某个量施加点名的倍数。

branches.en: MAKING MORE: swelling a number greatly, and swelling someone's chances.
branches.cn: 使更多：让数量大大增加，也让机会大大增加。

branches.en: BECOMING MANY: problems and troubles simply grow in number.
branches.cn: 自己变多：问题与麻烦就这样越来越多。

branches.en: LIFE COPIES ITSELF: rabbits breeding and cells dividing are the same arithmetic in flesh.
branches.cn: 生命复制自身：兔子繁殖与细胞分裂，是同一套算术长在血肉里。

branches.en: OPEN THE BRACKETS: multiply out unfolds the product term by term.
branches.cn: 打开括号：乘开把乘积一项一项地展开。

intro.en: Multiply is a Latin verb of folding many together; its pieces and endings build a large English family.
intro.cn: multiply 是一个拉丁动词，意为把许多层折在一起；其构件与词尾构成一个很大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin multus and plicare give multiple, multiplex, multiplicity, explicit, complicate and duplicate; the verb ending -are became English -ify through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 multus 与 plicare 衍生 multiple、multiplex、multiplicity、explicit、complicate 与 duplicate；动词词尾 -are 经法语变成英语的 -ify。

items.example: The first part says many.
items.exampleCN: 前半部分说的是「多」。

items.example: The second part says fold.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分说的是「折」。

items.example: The adjective stays in English as multiplex.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词以 multiplex 的形式留在英语里。

items.example: The Latin verb is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是直接来源。

items.meaning: to make a product; to increase
items.example: Multiply the two numbers.
items.exampleCN: 把这两个数相乘。

items.example: Multiplication is repeated addition.
items.exampleCN: 乘法是重复相加。

items.meaning: a number that contains another exactly
items.example: Six is a multiple of two.
items.exampleCN: 六是二的倍数。

items.example: The multiplicity of voices filled the room.
items.exampleCN: 众多声音充满了房间。

items.meaning: the number or factor that multiplies
items.example: The multiplier raised every score.
items.exampleCN: 这个乘数把每个分数都抬高了。

items.meaningCN: 表示「使成为」的动词后缀
items.example: It also appears in simplify and amplify.
items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 simplify 与 amplify 里。

definition_zh: 除法；分开；分配；部门；分歧；师；细胞分裂；分类单元
definition_en: the act of separating something into parts, the arithmetic operation of sharing into equal groups, or one of the parts so made
core_image: 一张饼被刀切成四份，每份大小相同地摆开
scene: 一张饼被刀分成四份，每份大小相同。The fair division of the cake gave every child an equal piece.
sceneCN: 这里 division 指「把整体分成若干等份的动作」（第 2 个义项：分开、分割）；句意为把蛋糕公平地分开，让每个孩子都得到一样大的一块。图中可辨识物件：蛋糕、刀、四块、伸出的手。

pos.zh: 除法；分开；分配；部门；分歧；师；分类单元

senses.title: The arithmetic operation
senses.definition: the operation of finding how many times one number is contained in another
senses.definitionCN: 求一个数里含有另一个数多少次的运算
senses.example: Long division broke the problem into a series of small subtractions.
senses.exampleCN: 竖式除法把这个问题拆成一连串小减法。
senses.why: division is literally a splitting: the dividend is cut into equal groups whose size the divisor fixes.
senses.whyCN: 除法字面上就是一次劈分：被除数被切成若干等份，每份的大小由除数定下。

senses.title: The act of separating
senses.definition: the process of cutting or separating something into parts
senses.definitionCN: 把某物切开或分成若干部分的过程
senses.example: The fair division of the cake gave every child an equal piece.
senses.exampleCN: 把蛋糕公平地分开，让每个孩子都得到一样大的一块。
senses.why: the oldest sense is physical: a whole is cut apart, and every later sense keeps that image.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是实物的：整体被切开，之后每个义项都保留这个形象。

senses.title: The sharing out of something
senses.definition: the distribution of something among several people or places
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分给若干人或若干地方
senses.example: The division of the profits was settled before the work began.
senses.exampleCN: 利润的分配在开工前就已定好。
senses.why: once a whole is cut, the pieces must be handed out, so division also names distribution.
senses.whyCN: 整体一旦切开，各块就得发下去，因此 division 也指分配。

senses.title: A branch of an organization
senses.definition: a separate unit of a company or institution with its own function
senses.definitionCN: 公司或机构中承担特定职能的独立单位
senses.example: The sales division moved to the building across the street.
senses.exampleCN: 销售部门搬到了街对面那栋楼。
senses.why: an organization is divided into units, and each unit is a piece cut from the whole.
senses.whyCN: 组织被分成若干单位，每个单位都是从整体上切下的一块。

senses.title: Disagreement that splits people
senses.definition: a state in which people are separated by opposing views
senses.definitionCN: 人们因对立观点而分成两边的状态
senses.example: The vote revealed a deep division within the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这次表决暴露了委员会内部的深刻分歧。
senses.why: a group that splits into sides is divided like a body cut in two, so the word covers social separation.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体分成两边，就像身体被切成两半，因此这个词也覆盖社会性的分离。

senses.title: A military division
senses.definition: a large military formation made of several regiments or brigades
senses.definitionCN: 由若干团或旅组成的大型军事编制
senses.example: The infantry division held the valley for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 这个步兵师守住了山谷三天。
senses.why: armies are organized by dividing troops into large formations, and each formation carries the name of that division.
senses.whyCN: 军队按把兵力分成大编制来组织，每个编制就带着「分割」的名字。

senses.title: Cell division
senses.definition: the process by which one cell splits into two
senses.definitionCN: 一个细胞分裂成两个的过程
senses.example: Cell division is how a single egg becomes a whole body.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞分裂就是一个卵细胞变成一个完整身体的方式。
senses.why: biology uses the literal image: one living unit cuts itself into two.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用的是字面形象：一个生命单位把自己切成两个。

senses.title: A rank in a sports league
senses.definition: one of the graded levels in which teams are grouped for competition
senses.definitionCN: 参赛队伍被分组比赛时所用的分级层次
senses.example: The club was promoted to the first division last season.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部上赛季升入了甲级。
senses.why: teams are divided into levels, and each level is called a division.
senses.whyCN: 球队被分成若干层次，每个层次就称为一个 division。

senses.title: A rank in plant classification
senses.definition: a taxonomic rank between kingdom and class in botany
senses.definitionCN: 植物分类中位于界与纲之间的一个分类等级
senses.example: The ferns form a division of their own in the plant kingdom.
senses.exampleCN: 蕨类在植物界中自成一个门。
senses.why: taxonomy divides living things into nested groups, and one of those levels is named after the dividing.
senses.whyCN: 分类学把生物分成层层嵌套的组，其中一个层级就以「分割」命名。

intro.en: Division comes from Latin divisio 'a dividing', from dividere 'to divide'. English took it through Old French, first as physical separation and later as the arithmetic operation.
intro.cn: division 来自拉丁 divisio「一次分割」，出自 dividere「分开」。英语经古法语引入，最初指实物分离，后来才指算术运算。

items.en: Dis- meant 'apart, in different directions'; it is the prefix that turns a single act into a separating one.
items.cn: dis- 意为「分开、朝不同方向」；这个前缀把单一动作变成分离的动作。

items.en: Dividere meant 'to force apart, divide'. The second element is usually connected with a root meaning 'to separate', but its exact pre-Latin shape is uncertain.
items.cn: dividere 意为「使分开、分割」。第二个构件通常与一个意为「分离」的词根相联系，但其拉丁语之前的确切形态并不确定。

items.en: Divisio, from the participle divisus, named the act or result of dividing.
items.cn: divisio 出自分词 divisus，命名分割的动作或结果。

items.en: Old French division brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century with the sense of separation and sharing.
items.cn: 古法语 division 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，意思是分离与分配。

items.en: The arithmetic sense appears in the late Middle Ages, while the organizational and military senses grew from the seventeenth century onward.
items.cn: 算术义出现在中世纪晚期，而组织义与军事义则从十七世纪以后发展起来。

items.en: Dates for the later specialized senses are approximate; Latin dividere and divisio are securely attested.
items.cn: 后来的专门义项年代为约数；拉丁 dividere 与 divisio 则有可靠记录。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for dividing and is easily confused; the second group names splitting and sharing.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「分开」的拉丁动词，容易混淆；第二组是分割与分配的说法。

entries.definition: The verb of the action; division is the noun naming the act or the result.
entries.definitionCN: 动作的动词；division 是命名动作或结果的名词。

entries.definition: Able to be divided, especially without a remainder; it describes a number, not the operation.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被整除的；描述一个数，不是运算本身。

entries.definition: Causing disagreement between people; it is the adjective of the social sense of division.
entries.definitionCN: 指造成人们分歧的；是 division 社会义的形容词。

entries.definition: From individuus 'indivisible', the negated form of dividere: one who cannot be cut apart.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 individuus「不可分的」，是 dividere 的否定形式：不能切开的一个存在。

entries.definition: The number to be divided, from dividendum 'that which is to be divided'; it is the input, not the operation.
entries.definitionCN: 指被除的数，来自 dividendum「该被分的东西」；是输入，不是运算。

entries.definition: The state of being apart; division stresses the act of cutting a whole into parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指分开的状态；division 强调把整体切成部分这个动作。

entries.definition: A division into parts or a wall that divides; it often refers to a physical or political split.
entries.definitionCN: 指分成若干部分，或分隔的墙；常指实体或政治上的分割。

entries.definition: A specialized unit of an organization; it is one common synonym for the branch sense of division.
entries.definitionCN: 指组织中的专门单位；是 division 部门义的一个常见同义词。

entries.definition: An informal word for a break or separation; division is the formal and general term.
entries.definitionCN: 指断裂或分开的口语词；division 是正式而一般的说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: dis- 'apart' plus a root for separating: a whole forced apart into pieces.
normal.cn: dis-「分开」加表分离的词根：整体被掰成若干块。

normal.en: The family runs divide, division, divisible, divisive and divisor.
normal.cn: 同族词有 divide、division、divisible、divisive 与 divisor。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: long division, sales division, cell division.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：竖式除法、销售部门、细胞分裂。

normal.en: The army, the company and the football club all split their people into divisions.
normal.cn: 军队、公司与足球俱乐部都把人员分成 division。

normal.cn: 竖式除法不过是重复相减，也就是重复切割。

abstract.cn: 想象一间大厅被一道矮墙分成两半，两边听不见彼此。

abstract.en: Picture a single cell pulling itself into two smaller cells.
abstract.cn: 想象一个细胞把自己拉成两个更小的细胞。

examples.en: The company created a new division to handle overseas sales.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「分」字打头——把整块分开，分成几份 → 除法、分割、部门

root: 拉丁 dis-（分开）+ dividere（分割）→ divisio「一次分割」→ 古法语 division → 英语 division。dividere 第二构件的更早形态不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all start with a cut: the arithmetic operation, physical separation, sharing out, an organizational branch, a split in opinion, a military formation, a dividing cell, a league level and a botanical rank.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都从一刀切开始：算术运算、实物分离、分配、组织部门、意见分裂、军事编制、分裂的细胞、联赛级别与植物分类等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cake cut into four equal pieces laid out side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个蛋糕被切成四等份，一块块摆开。

branches.en: THE CUT ITSELF: the arithmetic operation and the physical act of separating.
branches.cn: 切割本身：算术运算与实物的分离动作。

branches.en: SHARING OUT: once cut, the pieces are handed to different people.
branches.cn: 分下去：切开之后，各块被发给不同的人。

branches.en: BRANCHES AND FORMATIONS: a company unit and an army formation are both pieces cut from a larger body.
branches.cn: 分支与编制：公司的单位与军队的编制，都是从更大整体切下的一块。

branches.en: PEOPLE SPLIT: opposing views cut a group into two sides.
branches.cn: 人群分裂：对立观点把一群人切成两边。

branches.en: SPLITTING IN NATURE AND PLAY: a cell divides, a league divides into levels, and botany divides plants into ranks.
branches.cn: 生命与游戏里的分割：细胞分裂、联赛分级、植物分门。

intro.en: Division is a Latin action noun on the verb 'to divide'; the prefix, root and suffix all build English words.
intro.cn: division 是建立在「分开」动词上的拉丁动作名词；前缀、词根与后缀都构成英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin dividere gives divide, divisible, divisive, dividend and individual; the suffix -io, through French -ion, names the act or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dividere 衍生 divide、divisible、divisive、dividend 与 individual；后缀 -io 经法语 -ion 命名动作或结果。

items.example: The prefix turns one act into a separating one.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把单一动作变成分离的动作。

items.example: The verb is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The participle describes what has been split.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词描述已被分开的东西。

items.example: The noun names the cut itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名切割本身。

items.example: Division gave each child a piece.
items.exampleCN: 分蛋糕让每个孩子得到一块。

items.example: Divide the rope into two halves.
items.exampleCN: 把绳子分成两半。

items.example: Ten is divisible by five.
items.exampleCN: 十能被五整除。

items.example: The proposal was divisive.
items.exampleCN: 这个提案造成了分歧。

items.meaning: one that cannot be cut apart
items.example: Each individual has a vote.
items.exampleCN: 每个个人都有一票。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: It turns divide into division.
items.exampleCN: 它把 divide 变成 division。

definition_zh: 分开；分割；分配；除；使产生分歧；分水岭
definition_en: to separate something into parts, to share it out, or to perform the operation of division
core_image: 一根绳子在地上被拉直，中间做个记号，两边等长
scene: 绳子在地上被拉直，中间做了个记号，两边长度相同。They divide the rope into two equal lengths before the game.
sceneCN: 这里 divide 指「把某物切成若干部分」（第 2 个义项：分割成部分）；句意为比赛前他们把这根绳子分成等长的两段。图中可辨识物件：绳子、记号、地面、两只手。

pos.zh: 分开；分割；分配；除；使分歧
分水岭；分界

senses.title: To perform division
senses.definition: to find how many times one number is contained in another
senses.definitionCN: 求一个数里含有另一个数多少次
senses.example: Divide the total by the number of days to find the daily average.
senses.exampleCN: 用总数除以天数，就得到每日平均值。
senses.why: the verb is the act behind division: a quantity is cut into equal groups whose size the divisor sets.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是除法背后的动作：一个量被切成等份，每份大小由除数决定。

senses.title: To separate into parts
senses.definition: to cut or break something into two or more pieces
senses.definitionCN: 把某物切或分成两块或更多块
senses.example: They divide the rope into two equal lengths before the game.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前他们把这根绳子分成等长的两段。
senses.why: the physical sense is the oldest: a whole is forced apart, and the arithmetic sense is that same cut made exact.
senses.whyCN: 实物义最古老：整体被掰开，而算术义只是把这一刀切得更精确。

senses.title: To share out among people
senses.definition: to give portions of something to different people
senses.definitionCN: 把某物的若干份给不同的人
senses.example: The teacher divided the books among the four groups.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把书分给四个小组。
senses.why: after a whole is cut, the pieces are handed out, so the verb covers distribution as well as splitting.
senses.whyCN: 整体切开之后，各块要发下去，因此这个动词既指切开，也指分配。

senses.title: To sort into categories
senses.definition: to arrange things into groups according to a rule
senses.definitionCN: 按某种规则把事物归入不同组别
senses.example: The librarian divides the collection into fiction and reference.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆员把藏书分成小说与工具书。
senses.why: classification is a division by kind: things are cut apart along the lines of their differences.
senses.whyCN: 分类就是按种类分割：事物沿着差异的界线被切开。

senses.title: To set people against each other
senses.definition: to cause disagreement or hostility between people
senses.definitionCN: 在人们之间造成分歧或敌意
senses.example: The new rule divided the neighbours into two camps.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定把邻居们分成了两个阵营。
senses.why: when opinions split, the group is literally divided, so the same verb describes social separation.
senses.whyCN: 当意见分裂时，群体就被劈成两半，因此同一个动词也描述社会性的分离。

senses.title: The watershed between two rivers
senses.definition: the ridge of land that separates the drainage of two river systems
senses.definitionCN: 分隔两个水系排水方向的山脊
senses.example: Rain on one side of the divide reaches the Pacific, rain on the other reaches the Atlantic.
senses.exampleCN: 分水岭一侧的雨水流入太平洋，另一侧的雨水流入大西洋。
senses.why: the noun divide names the line where water is split into two directions, a purely geographical cutting.
senses.whyCN: 名词 divide 命名水被分成两个方向的那条线，是一次纯粹地理上的切割。

senses.title: To partition a space
senses.definition: to separate an area with a wall, screen or other barrier
senses.definitionCN: 用墙、屏风或其他屏障把一块区域分隔开
senses.example: A low shelf divides the studio from the sleeping area.
senses.exampleCN: 一道矮书架把工作室与睡觉的地方隔开。
senses.why: a room divided is a whole cut by a barrier, exactly the physical image of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 被分隔的房间就是被屏障切开的一个整体，正是这个动词的实物形象。

senses.title: To divide up
senses.definition: to distribute all of something among the people involved
senses.definitionCN: 把所有东西分给相关的人
senses.example: They divided up the remaining work and finished by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把剩下的工作分摊掉，中午就完成了。
senses.why: the particle 'up' marks the completion of the cutting: nothing is left whole.
senses.whyCN: 「分掉」里的「掉」标出切割的完成：没有东西再保持完整。

intro.en: Divide comes from Latin dividere 'to force apart', built on dis- 'apart' plus a second element of uncertain shape. English took the verb through Old French divider.
intro.cn: divide 来自拉丁 dividere「使分开」，由 dis-「分开」加一个形态不确定的第二构件构成。英语经古法语 divider 引入这个动词。

items.en: Dis- meant 'apart, asunder'. It is the prefix of separation in many Latin verbs and their English children.
items.cn: dis- 意为「分开、散开」。它是许多拉丁动词及其英语后代里的分离前缀。

items.en: Dividere meant 'to force apart, divide'. The second element is usually linked with a root meaning 'to separate', but the exact pre-Latin form is uncertain and the proposed shapes are reconstructions.
items.cn: dividere 意为「使分开、分割」。第二个构件通常与一个意为「分离」的词根相联系，但其拉丁语之前的确切形态不确定，所提出的形态属于重构。

items.en: The past participle divisus 'divided' produced the noun divisio and the later adjective forms.
items.cn: 过去分词 divisus「被分开的」产生了名词 divisio 与后来的形容词形式。

items.en: Old French divider carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century, first as physical separation and sharing.
items.cn: 古法语 divider 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语，最初指实物分离与分配。

items.en: The mathematical sense developed in the late Middle Ages alongside written calculation, and the noun divide for a watershed followed in geography.
items.cn: 数学义在中世纪晚期随笔算发展起来，而表示分水岭的名词 divide 则在地理学中随后出现。

items.en: The first date for the geographical noun is approximate; the deeper shape of the Latin root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 地理名词的最早年代为约数；这个拉丁词根更深层的形态属于来源不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb and is easily confused; the second group names separating and sharing without the arithmetic sense.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个拉丁动词，容易混淆；第二组是表示分离与分配、但不含算术义的说法。

entries.definition: The noun of the action; divide is the verb that performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 动作的名词；divide 是执行这个动作的动词。

entries.definition: Able to be divided without a remainder; it describes a number, not an action.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被整除的；描述一个数，不是动作。

entries.definition: Causing a split among people; it is the adjective matching the social sense of divide.
entries.definitionCN: 指在人群中造成分裂的；对应 divide 的社会义。

entries.definition: The number to be divided; it is the object of the action rather than the action.
entries.definitionCN: 指被除的数；它是动作的对象，不是动作本身。

entries.definition: From individuus 'not divisible': a single being that cannot be cut apart.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 individuus「不可分的」：一个不能切开的单独存在。

entries.definition: To put apart things that were together; it stresses distance rather than equal portions.
entries.definitionCN: 指把原本在一起的东西分开；强调距离，而非等份。

entries.definition: To break or cut apart, often abruptly; divide is the more formal and general verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指劈开或断开，常带突然感；divide 是更正式、更一般的动词。

entries.definition: To give portions to others; it covers the distribution sense of divide without the cutting.
entries.definitionCN: 指把份额给别人；覆盖 divide 的分配义，但不含切割。

entries.definition: To divide an area or a state into parts, often with a barrier or a treaty.
entries.definitionCN: 指把区域或国家分成若干部分，常通过屏障或条约。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: dis- 'apart' plus the dividing root: to force a whole into pieces.
normal.cn: dis-「分开」加表分割的词根：把整体掰成若干块。

normal.en: The family runs divide, division, divisible, divisive, divisor and dividend.
normal.cn: 同族词有 divide、division、divisible、divisive、divisor 与 dividend。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: divide into, divide by, divide up.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：分成、除以、分掉。

normal.en: A continental divide splits the rain, just as a knife splits a cake.
normal.cn: 大陆分水岭把雨水分开，正如刀把蛋糕分开。

normal.en: The verb and the noun divide name the same cut, one as action and one as the ridge it leaves.
normal.cn: 动词与名词 divide 命名同一刀切，一个是动作，一个是留下的脊线。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled tight and marked exactly in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子绷直，正中做了一个记号。

abstract.en: Picture a room cut in two by a thin screen, each side unable to see the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子被一层薄屏风切成两半，两边看不见彼此。

abstract.en: Picture rain falling on a ridge and running away in two directions.
abstract.cn: 想象雨落在山脊上，向两个方向流走。

examples.en: Divide twelve by three and the answer is four.
examples.cn: 十二除以三，答案是四。

examples.en: The river divides the old town into two distinct quarters.
examples.cn: 这条河把老城分成两个截然不同的街区。

examples.en: They divided up the land equally among the families.
examples.cn: 他们把土地平均分给各家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「分开」的音——把东西分成几份 → 分开、除

root: 拉丁 dis-（分开）+ dividere（分割）→ 古法语 divider → 英语 divide。dividere 第二构件的更早形态不确定，相关形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one cut: the arithmetic operation, physical splitting, sharing out, sorting into kinds, setting people apart, a watershed, partitioning a room and distributing everything.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一刀：算术运算、实物劈分、分配、归类、使人群分裂、分水岭、隔开房间，以及把所有东西分掉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope pulled straight, marked at the middle, both halves equal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绳子拉直，中间做了记号，两半等长。

branches.en: THE CUT ITSELF: the arithmetic operation and the physical act of splitting.
branches.cn: 切割本身：算术运算与实物的劈分动作。

branches.en: SHARING OUT: giving portions, and distributing all of it until nothing is whole.
branches.cn: 分下去：把份额给出，直到没有东西保持完整。

branches.en: SORT INTO KINDS: classification cuts a collection along the lines of difference.
branches.cn: 归类：分类沿着差异的界线把一堆东西切开。

branches.en: PEOPLE SET APART: an opinion splits a group into camps.
branches.cn: 人群被分开：一种意见把群体切成阵营。

branches.en: LINES IN LAND AND ROOMS: a watershed splits the rain, a screen splits a studio.
branches.cn: 土地与房间里的界线：分水岭分开雨水，屏风分开工作室。

intro.en: Divide is a Latin verb of separation; its prefix and root also build division, divisible and individual.
intro.cn: divide 是一个表示分离的拉丁动词；其前缀与词根还构成 division、divisible 与 individual。

latinIntro.en: Latin dividere gives division, divisible, divisive, dividend, divisor and individual; the prefix dis- marks separation throughout.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dividere 衍生 division、divisible、divisive、dividend、divisor 与 individual；前缀 dis- 始终标记分离。

items.example: The prefix does the separating.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀负责分离。

items.example: The Latin verb is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是直接来源。

items.example: Divide the work among the team.
items.exampleCN: 把工作分给团队。

items.meaning: the act or result of dividing

items.exampleCN: 分工加快工作。

items.example: Nine is divisible by three.
items.exampleCN: 九能被三整除。

items.example: The issue proved divisive.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题造成了分裂。

items.example: The dividend is written inside the bracket.
items.exampleCN: 被除数写在除号里面。

items.example: The divisor stands outside the bracket.
items.exampleCN: 除数写在除号外面。

items.exampleCN: 它也构成 visible 与 possible。
